articles.title: Omar Cooper Jr. and the Best Week 8 Fantasy Football Waiver-Wire Pickups
articles.summary: With Week 8 on the horizon, the 2026 fantasy football season is rounding past the halfway point. This may be the time of year when serviceable waiver options start to dry up, but the free-agent pool shouldn't be completely bereft of potential league-winners quite yet.
articles.body:
With Week 8 on the horizon, the 2026 fantasy football season is rounding past the halfway point. This may be the time of year when serviceable waiver options start to dry up, but the free-agent pool shouldn't be completely bereft of potential league-winners quite yet.

Whether they stand to benefit from a starter's injury or are returning from IR themselves, several players who remain widely available in fantasy leagues appear poised to play significant roles in Week 8.

The upcoming NFL trade deadline could also reshape the fantasy landscape. A handful of blockbuster deals have gone down in recent years involving big-name talents, moves that opened the door for backups and lesser-used players to step into the spotlight.

Even if your team is sitting atop the standings with quality starters and good depth, it can still pay dividends to stash a player who could see a huge increase in playing time if the trendy trade candidate ahead of him does end up getting dealt prior to the Nov. 10 deadline.

With that in mind, here's a look at the top waiver-wire targets for Week 8.

Suggestions are available in approximately half or more of all Yahoo! Sports leagues. Fantasy points and rankings courtesy of FantasyPros ' PPR data. Suggested free-agent acquisition budget (FAAB) bids are based on a $100 starting budget.

Baker Mayfield, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (25 Percent Rostered)

Mayfield's Week 7 return coincided with a massive 43-13 win over the Carolina Panthers, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback was sparingly utilized in the blowout contest. He only let 11 passes rip, completing seven of them for 64 yards and a touchdown.

While Tampa didn't need the veteran passer to contribute much in that convincing victory over a divisional rival, he is unlikely to attempt so few passes regularly.

The 31-year-old was averaging 32 throws per game in 2026 prior to picking up a thumb injury that cost him three contests and had never recorded fewer than 18 passing attempts in any of his previous 123 career starts.

With top wideout Emeka Egbuka likely to be back in the lineup after missing Week 7 with a concussion, the Bucs will air it out frequently against an Atlanta Falcons defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league in fantasy points allowed to opposing QBs.

It's an ideal opportunity for Mayfield to return to form after thus far failing to record a top-20 finish in 2026.

Michael Penix Jr., Atlanta Falcons (18 Percent Rostered)

An abysmal start to the 2026 campaign set the Falcons offense back, but this unit has found new life with Penix at the reins. The third-year quarterback just orchestrated a pivotal 29-20 win over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, putting up 20.4 fantasy points in the process.

Although Penix didn't look too sharp upon returning from an extended absence due to his latest ACL tear in 2025, he's dialed it in over the past two weeks and has now posted back-to-back top-10 finishes. The 26-year-old has tallied six touchdown passes in that span and has a real shot at putting up several more scores when the Falcons visit the Bucs in Week 8.

J.J. McCarthy, New York Giants (11 Percent Rostered)

McCarthy may have cemented his status as Big Blue's starter for the remainder of 2026 by leading the Giants past the Houston Texans, but the third-year signal-caller only mustered 10.2 points in the 27-21 overtime victory.

McCarthy's eye-popping Week 6 production (17.3 points in just one quarter) was clearly unsustainable, but his showing this past weekend may wind up being his floor. He completed a respectable 20 of 28 throws for 252 yards and avoided turnovers, but a lack of touchdown passes and only a single rushing yard greatly hindered his fantasy output.

The G-Men are now heading into a Week 8 bye, giving McCarthy further opportunity to develop within this rejuvenated offense.

Deep league managers (and even those in standard formats who will have a starting QB on bye in Weeks 9 or 10) should consider securing a spot on their bench for McCarthy.

A pair of favorable matchups against the Philadelphia Eagles and Washington Commanders right out of the break makes him a high-upside plug-and-play option for those weeks.

Jonah Coleman, Denver Broncos (35 Percent Rostered)

Coleman's 8.9-point performance in his first game back from an IR stint may not look too promising at a glance, but he's a top priority waiver-wire target for Week 8 due to his potential to seize control of Denver's backfield.

With RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins both failing to distinguish themselves during Coleman's four-game layoff, the rookie returned to lead the group in offensive snaps by a wide margin.

Although he didn't score like his two platoonmates, Coleman tallied 54 rushing yards on nine totes and added 15 receiving yards with his two catches. The fourth-rounder was more effective on the ground than both Dobbins (6/23/1) and Harvey (3/6/0) and was only outperformed by Harvey as a receiver due to the 52-yard scoring reception the latter created on one of his two catches.

Coleman was Denver's preferred choice to grind out clock late in the contest and appears poised for even more volume in the back half of the campaign. Sean Payton said after Sunday's game that Coleman "looked really good" and that the coaching staff has "got to get him more touches" going forward.

That upside makes Coleman a must-add in nearly every format. If he can stay healthy, Coleman will be a borderline RB2 down the stretch and greatly aid managers desperate for production at the position.

Seth McGowan, Indianapolis Colts (7 Percent Rostered)

Rumors are swirling that the Colts will become sellers at the upcoming NFL trade deadline due to a disappointing 2-5 start to the 2026 season.

One of the most obvious candidates to be moved is Jonathan Taylor, the team's elite running back. If he is dealt, his departure would instantly elevate McGowan to the cusp of fantasy stardom.

McGowan has flashed an impressive level of talent in limited action, racking up 146 yards on his first 36 career touches. Playing time has kept him from breaking out, however, as the rookie has only seen the field for 98 offensive snaps . Taylor has unsurprisingly earned the lion's share of playing time and touches, amassing 765 yards and eight touchdowns on 157 touches across 374 offensive snaps .

With little in the way of competition—DJ Giddens is the only other RB on the roster, but the third-stringer hasn't logged a single snap this season—McGowan projects to step directly into Taylor's lead back role. This herculean upside, as well as his current handcuff value, makes McGowan one of the top players you can stash. Don't hesitate to scoop him up and hold him through the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Dylan Sampson, Cleveland Browns (8 Percent Rostered)

Sampson returned to action on Sunday after missing the last five games with a knee injury. The Browns wasted little time getting him involved, as the second-year back finished the Week 7 win over the Tennessee Titans with 45 rushing yards on six carries and 32 receiving yards on three catches.

Although Sampson won't always put up double-digit fantasy points or post borderline top-25 finishes when he's logging less than 10 touches, he looked healthy and was highly productive as the No. 2 back behind Quinshon Judkins.

Considering Judkins has had injury woes of his own—he missed Week 6 with an ankle issue—this pickup has both flex appeal and handcuff value.

Bam Knight, Arizona Cardinals (25 Percent Rostered)

Knight has stepped up and delivered some strong performances while filling in for injured rookie Jeremiyah Love.

Despite facing a pair of teams with tough defensive fronts in the Los Angeles Rams and Denver Broncos over the last two weeks, the veteran has generated 161 yards from scrimmage and scored over 20 fantasy points in that span.

Although upside is limited here due to Arizona's lack of scoring prowess and a timeshare with Tyler Allgeier, managers in the market for a one-week RB rental could do worse than claiming Knight off waivers.

Be sure to monitor the latest injury news before you deploy him, however, as Love remains week-to-week. If the first-round rookie is back for Arizona's upcoming clash against the Dallas Cowboys, Knight would become a much riskier fantasy option.

Omar Cooper Jr., New York Jets (48 Percent Rostered)

Cooper burst onto the fantasy scene with a 22.3-point outing in Week 6 and showed no signs of slowing down Sunday.

The Jets' rookie phenom continued his hot streak by putting up 115 receiving yards and a touchdown on five catches, a 22.5-point performance that resulted in a second consecutive top-10 finish.

Since battling through an ankle injury suffered on his first NFL touch and subsequently spending a month on the IR, Cooper has become a revelation for a talent-starved Jets squad.

Although he couldn't spur Gang Green to a victory over the AFC East rival Miami Dolphins, the team would have fared far worse without the first-rounder making several big plays.

Expect Cooper to continue along his rising star trajectory when New York faces the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 8.

Vegas has allowed an average of 21.8 fantasy points per game to opposing wideouts and has been lit up by several pass-catchers during its current four-game losing skid. Cooper should feast against a slumping secondary, earning him priority target status on waivers.

KC Concepcion, Cleveland Browns (60 Percent Rostered)

Concepcion may be owned in a bit more than half of all leagues, but it's worth checking if he is up for grabs in yours.

While the Cleveland rookie got off to a slow start to his NFL career, the first-round pick finally had his long-awaited breakout game on Sunday. In a 27-24 win over the Tennessee Titans, he hauled in eight of 10 targets for 129 receiving yards and added 23 rushing yards on three carries.

Concepcion's top-10 finish was impressive, but managers may understandably doubt he can repeat the feat in the wake of six straight WR39 or worse showings.

His team-high 45 targets demonstrate that he has received ample opportunity and suggest he will remain heavily involved. Despite his inconsistent production, consider him a high-upside WR3 who could deliver more consistent numbers in the coming weeks.

Antonio Williams, Washington Commanders (8 Percent Rostered)

The Commanders have a major void to fill in their receiving corps after Terry McLaurin's season ended in Week 6 with a torn patellar tendon. Williams should get the first crack at replacing the veteran star when Washington comes out of a fortunately timed Week 7 bye.

While Williams has had a solid but unspectacular start to his NFL career (recording 18 catches for 205 yards and one touchdown in six games), he's now a true breakout candidate.

The third-round rookie was already seeing an uptick in playing time before McLaurin's injury and clearly has the skills and athleticism to work as McLaurin's direct replacement.

Some risk comes with inserting Williams directly into a Week 8 starting lineup, but he's at least worth stashing in most formats and could pay dividends if he reaches his lofty ceiling.

Caleb Douglas, Miami Dolphins (13 Percent Rostered)

Douglas was an intriguing waiver addition following his WR22 finish in the opener, but the rookie went down in Week 2 with an ankle sprain that sidelined him through Miami's Week 6 bye.

In his first game back, Douglas exploded for a career-high 21 fantasy points. He secured a pair of touchdown grabs, including a highlight-worthy 63-yard catch-and-run late in the fourth quarter that pushed the 'Phins into the win column for the first time this season.

While most of Douglas' production was tied to his two scores, he should see a rapid increase in both offensive snaps and targets as he reintegrates himself in Miami's offense. He's a high-risk, high-reward waiver option for WR-needy managers going into Week 8.

Hunter Henry, New England Patriots (56 Percent Rostered)

Henry continued his hot streak during New England's loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. While his side came up short in the 30-24 defeat, he remained one of Drake Maye's go-to targets and rewarded fantasy managers with another good outing.

Although Henry failed to find pay dirt for the first time since Week 4, he still caught all seven of his targets for 71 yards to salvage his fantasy day. That 14.1-point effort marked his fourth consecutive double-digit performance and his third consecutive top-10 finish.

Despite this steady production at a position largely bereft of serviceable waiver-wire options, Henry is still available in nearly half of all fantasy leagues. He should be rostered in far more than that, so be sure to add him if he's still somehow lingering in your free-agent scrap heap.

Terrance Ferguson, Los Angeles Rams (15 Percent Rostered)

The desperate Rams started turning things around with a much-needed win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7. Their offense looked sharp in the 35-21 victory and will soon get even more dangerous due to the impending return of Ferguson.

Ferguson is eligible to come off the IR and could be back on the field in time for a Week 8 showdown against the SoFi Stadium rival Los Angeles Chargers. His presence will provide a significant boost to L.A.'s overextended tight end unit, one that has needed to cover for the injuries the team's receiving corps is contending with.

Davis Allen hauled in two of Matt Stafford's three touchdown throws against the Raiders and Colby Parkinson (5/48/0 on six targets) was the team's second-most productive pass-catcher in the contest, but Ferguson figures to usurp both in the pecking order when he's back in the lineup. Scoop him up for TE1 upside if you don't have a stable starter.

Chig Okonkwo, Washington Commanders (17 Percent Rostered)

Okonkwo had been steadily establishing himself as a reliable weapon in Washington's offense, but he became one of its focal points following Terry McLaurin's early exit during a Week 6 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers.

Okonkwo had his best game in a Commanders uniform in Week 6, hauling in all seven of his targets for 69 receiving yards. It resulted in a second consecutive top-15 finish, following on the heels of his six-target, four-catch, 60-yard receiving outing in Week 5.

While Okonkwo missed two games with injury and has yet to secure a touchdown catch in 2026, he's in line for plenty of looks as Washington works to redistribute the 6.5 targets McLaurin had been averaging prior to Week 6.

That should result in the type of steady production that puts Okonkwo right on the TE1 border.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley and 6 Other Players Eagles Should Move at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline After Latest Loss
articles.summary: Following Monday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys, the Philadelphia Eagles should pivot their focus to the future. General manager Howie Roseman could trade older veterans and players on expiring contracts for draft capital before the November 10 deadline.
articles.body:
Following Monday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys, the Philadelphia Eagles should pivot their focus to the future. General manager Howie Roseman could trade older veterans and players on expiring contracts for draft capital before the November 10 deadline.

At 2-5, without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, who's dealing with blood clots, the Eagles are unlikely to make a run at a playoff spot. Keep in mind that 14-year starting right tackle Lane Johnson retired after Week 4. Soon after that, Philadelphia traded two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens.

Philadelphia doesn't need a full roster reset, but it makes sense to gauge the trade value of players who aren't part of the team's long-term plans.

We'll start with star running back Saquon Barkley, who's banged up but has been in the trade rumor mill.

The Eagles have Saquon Barkley under contract for two more seasons, but he turns 30 in February. General manager Howie Roseman can get ahead of the star running back's potential decline by trading him this year.

Barkley has already missed two games with a hamstring injury and didn't finish the last outing because of a back injury. He's running behind an offensive line that lost two starters early this month, Lane Johnson and Cam Jurgens, so the three-time Pro Bowler will probably struggle in Philadelphia for the remainder of the season.

With the possibility that Barkley's trade value takes a hit after a lackluster 2026 campaign, the Eagles could try to trade him now to maximize their return.

The Athletic's Zach Berman believes the Eagles will have "tougher debates" about how to handle Barkley's situation if they receive strong trade offers, but if a running back-needy team like the Minnesota Vikings calls with an aggressive proposal, Roseman should at least listen to the pitch.

While Barkley is probably the least likely of the Eagles' trade candidates to be moved, he would likely bring the most value in return if he's healthy enough to play in the short term.

Like Saquon Barkley, Zack Baun is a key contributor from the Eagles' 2024 Super Bowl team. After four years mostly as a backup with the New Orleans Saints, he revived his career in Philadelphia and became an All-Pro, Pro Bowl-caliber playmaker as the centerpiece of Vic Fangio's defense.

However, Baun will be 30 in December, and the Eagles selected linebacker Jihaad Campbell in the first round of the 2025 draft. The second-year pro leads the team in tackles and is establishing himself alongside Baun.

If the Eagles are open to trading Baun, they could elevate 2024 fifth-rounder Jeremiah Trotter Jr. to a larger role, then reassess the position before the 2027 draft.

Baun is still one of the league's top linebackers in coverage, allowing a 72.6 passer rating. He's a three-down defender, but because of his age and Campbell's emergence, Philadelphia may be willing to trade the two-time Pro Bowler.

Philadelphia signed Hollywood Brown to a one-year, $5 million deal this past offseason. He enjoyed his most productive seasons in 2021 and 2022 with the Baltimore Ravens and Arizona Cardinals, respectively, recording at least 67 catches and 709 receiving yards in each campaign.

At this stage in Brown's career, he could be a solid No. 3 target. In 2025, with the Kansas City Chiefs, the eighth-year pro hauled in 49 passes for 587 yards and five touchdowns, but he's only been active for two games in Philadelphia.

Unless DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) are out for an extended period, Brown is the most likely candidate on this list to be traded before the deadline.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers are calling around the league for wide receiver help. The Eagles could trade Brown back to the Chiefs or move him across Pennsylvania to Pittsburgh.

Predicting Five Potential Shocking Trades 😲

Dallas Goedert hasn't played through a full season since his 2018 rookie campaign. He's missed 11 games over the past three years, including two this season due to a sprained MCL.

Goedert will turn 32 by the end of the season. His long-term future in Philadelphia is uncertain, especially with rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers on the roster.

The Eagles activated Stowers from injured reserve for the previous game. He's a raw tight end talent who has to make up for lost time, but the 23-year-old can make plays in the passing game.

Over his last three years in college, Stowers caught 146 passes for 1,773 yards and 11 touchdowns. If his pass-catching ability translates to the pro level, he would be a solid replacement for Goedert, who was also a second-round pick in his draft class.

Following a solid 2025 season with 38 tackles (six for loss) and 21 pressures , Moro Ojomo generated buzz as a player who could get an extension, but the Eagles signed fellow defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter to multiyear deals.

The Eagles have Davis and Carter on the books for the next four years, so it's unlikely they'll sign a third defensive tackle to a lucrative multiyear contract.

In six contests, Ojomo has 13 tackles (two for loss) and nine pressures. Although his sack rate is down, he's a solid interior defensive lineman who plays 61 percent of the defensive snaps .

Ojomo could draw interest from a team like the Green Bay Packers, who lost defensive tackle Javon Hargrave (torn Achilles) for the season.

This past offseason, the Eagles acquired Dontayvion Wicks from the Green Bay Packers to remodel their wide receiver corps prior to trading A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots.

Wicks started the season strong, catching seven passes for 147 yards and a touchdown in the first two weeks, then had a couple of quiet outings in losses to the Chicago Bears and Los Angeles Rams. He caught five passes for 63 yards in Week 5, then struggled with backup quarterback Tanner McKee under center in Week 6.

Wicks didn't suit up Monday night because of an ankle injury. He'll be without his starting quarterback for the rest of the season, which will likely limit his production.

Philadelphia also traded up for Makai Lemon in the first round of this year's draft. He had a solid Monday night performance, catching seven passes for 67 yards and a touchdown. Darius Cooper recently emerged as a viable deep threat and red-zone target. With DeVonta Smith leading the receiver corps, the Eagles would have a solid trio of wideouts without Wicks.

With 19 receptions for 284 yards and a touchdown in six games, Wicks could attract trade suitors looking for a solid No. 2 receiver. Roseman could get a middle-round pick for him.

Philadelphia's 27th-ranked pass defense has struggled, and Riq Woolen's coverage has declined compared to his four years with the Seattle Seahawks.

Woolen has allowed two touchdowns and a 100 passer rating in coverage. In each of his four seasons with the Seahawks, he allowed passer ratings below 80.

The Eagles signed Woolen to a one-year deal, so trading him wouldn't shake up their secondary long term. They can move him and elevate 11-year veteran Jonathan Jones into a starting role on the perimeter, where he's lined up most in recent seasons.

As a 27-year-old, 6'4" cornerback with length, Woolen should be able to fetch a middle-round pick on the trade block.

Player contract details are provided by Spotrac .

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Dante Moore won’t quit on Oregon, but concussion will keep star QB out of games moving forward for Ducks
articles.summary: Dan Lanning confirmed Dante Moore won't return this season due to his concussion, shifting the Oregon quarterback's focus to the 2026 NFL Draft.
articles.body: The unfortunate 2026 season for the Oregon Ducks continues to get worse by the day, as Dan Lanning announced on Monday that he does not expect quarterback Dante Moore to return this season. It was during the September 28th game against USC when Oregon's season took a turn, when Moore sustained a concussion after taking a shot to the head by linebacker Desman Stephens as the quarterback was attempting to slide on a run. LINCOLN RILEY'S USC TENURE COULD END WITH LOSS AGAINST OHIO STATE'S BACKUP QUARTERBACK, WITH $70 MILLION BUYOUT LOOMING Over the past few weeks, Moore had returned to practice for Oregon, participating with the team on a daily basis. But, in terms of returning to the field in an uncontrolled environment, Dan Lanning mentioned that he can not be cleared by the Ducks medical team for a return to live action. "Really got clarity for us over the past week. I think if it was up to Dante in any shape or way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys," Lanning said on Monday. "But unfortunately, it's not really up to Dante, and it's not really up to me. We can control the settting of practice where he's able to do things for us, where that's not always the case in a game. "You know, we said before that this is a serious deal that he'll 100% be able to make a full recovery from. That has not changed, I definitely feel that way. But for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that's not going to happen." MORE QUESTIONS THAN ANSWERS: ARCH MANNING LIKES THE DISRESPECT, BIG 12'S DISASTER AND A CFP RACE IN DISARRAY This was not Dante Moore quitting on a three-loss Oregon team Up until the concussion sustained against USC, Moore had thrown for 925 yards and nine touchdowns, with zero interceptions. And, for those that think this was a decision Dante Moore made in relation to Oregon currently having three losses and the season being a wash, Lanning made it clear this was not the case, as Moore is currently the scout team quarterback. "We're getting one of the best scout team looks in practice every week, and he looks good out there," Lanning mentioned. "This isn’t like a selfish decision on Dante's part saying 'I don't wanna come back, the season doesn’t look like theyw ay I want it to look'. That's not at all what this is." USC LINEBACKER SUSPENDED AFTER VICIOUS HIT ON OREGON QUARTERBACK DANTE MOORE Oregon moving forward, with Dante Moore now preparing for the NFL The unfortunate situation for the Ducks quarterback has obviously had an effect over the past month. After suffering a loss to Oklahoma State, the Ducks were already working at a deficit in the eyes of CFP committee members, not being able to afford two more losses. But, as Oregon worked through two-different quarterbacks in Moore's absence, Dan Lanning has been dealt two additional losses in the process. Oregon committed seven turnovers in a 17-15 loss to UCLA earlier this month in a loss, and then this past weekend against Illinois could only score ten points in the 21-10 loss on the road. OREGON HEAD COACH DAN LANNING'S WORDS IMMEDIATELY CAME BACK TO BITE HIM IN AWFUL LOSS TO UCLA Now, the reality has set in for a football team that has not been able to establish a rushing attack, while dwindling in the passing game behind their backup quarterbacks. This led to Dan Lanning making the move to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. For Dante Moore, his focus will now shift to making a full recovery in preparation what comes next, which is expected to be the NFL Draft. The Oregon quarterback has been projected to be a first-round pick next April, after choosing to return for another season in Eugene this past offseason. What was once a season full of hope for Oregon has now turned into a disaster with over one month left in the regular season, as the Ducks are currently 4-3 with a very low percentage chance of making the postseason. There will be a lot of questions to be answered over the next few months before the transfer portal opens and Oregon starts to rebuild its roster for 2027, with Dylan Raiola transferring from Nebraska this past offseason in hopes of one day becoming the full-time starter in Eugene. articles.title: Every Super Bowl halftime show headliner from 2020 to 2027: From Shakira and Jennifer Lopez to Jay-Z
articles.summary: Jay-Z will headline Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium on February 14, 2027, the NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced on Monday, October 26.
articles.body: Jay-Z will headline Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium on February 14, 2027, the NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced on Monday, October 26. It ends a long wait for a man who has shaped this stage from the background since 2019. He joins a list that runs from Shakira and Jennifer Lopez through The Weeknd, Rihanna, Usher, Kendrick Lamar and Bad Bunny. Here is every headliner, what each show did, and where halftime is heading.All the headliners of the Super Bowl halftime show from 2020 to 2027Eight shows are now done or scheduled. Shakira and Jennifer Lopez played Super Bowl LIV in Miami in 2020. The Weeknd took Tampa in 2021. In 2022, Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige and Kendrick Lamar shared the SoFi Stadium stage. Rihanna followed in Glendale in 2023, then Usher in Las Vegas in 2024. Lamar came back alone in New Orleans in 2025, and Bad Bunny played Santa Clara in 2026. Jay-Z closes the run in 2027.One thing ties them together. Roc Nation has curated the show through an NFL deal that began in 2019 and was renewed in 2024.2020: Shakira and Jennifer Lopez turned Miami into a Latin partyThe February 2 show at Hard Rock Stadium split the time between two stars, then merged them. Shakira brought "Hips Don't Lie" and her belly dancing. Lopez answered with "Jenny from the Block" and a pole routine that dominated the next day's chatter. Bad Bunny and J Balvin dropped in as guests, and Lopez's daughter Emme sang as well.It was a loud statement of Latin pride. It also drew complaints to the FCC, a reminder that a show built for 100 million people never pleases all of them.2021: The Weeknd bet on mood over guestsSuper Bowl LV came during the pandemic, with a thinned-out crowd. The Weeknd started in the stands, moved through a maze of mirrors and lights, and surrounded himself with dancers in bandaged faces. He reportedly put about $7 million of his own money into the production.There were no guest stars. That choice mattered, because it proved one artist and a strong idea could carry the whole slot.2022: Hip-hop got its long-awaited halftimeSuper Bowl LVI at SoFi Stadium felt like a family reunion with a stadium budget. Dre, Snoop, Eminem, Blige and Lamar were joined by 50 Cent and Anderson .Paak. Eminem took a knee at the end of his set, a small gesture that drew big attention. The show later collected Emmy wins and set a template of a West Coast celebration that stayed rooted in place.2023 and 2024: Rihanna and Usher won on simplicityRihanna played Glendale on February 12, 2023, her first major live show in years. She floated above the field on suspended platforms in red, ran through her hits without a single guest, and revealed her pregnancy. She drew about 121 million viewers.Usher followed on February 11, 2024, in Las Vegas. He skated through a medley and brought out Alicia Keys, Lil Jon, Ludacris, Jermaine Dupri, will.i.am and H.E.R. His audience reached 123.4 million.Both relied on deep catalogues of songs people already knew. Neither tried to reinvent the format.2025: Kendrick Lamar made the biggest halftime everLamar became the first solo rapper to headline. His set at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans beat Michael Jackson's 1993 record. The final count was 133.5 million viewers, narrowly ahead of Jackson's 133.4 million. SZA, Mustard and Serena Williams joined him, and Samuel L. Jackson narrated as Uncle Sam. The "Not Like Us" moment, with its sly build, was what everyone replayed.What stood out was restraint. The staging was clean and the message did the heavy lifting.2026: Bad Bunny made Spanish the main languageThe Levi's Stadium show on February 8 was the first halftime headlined by a Latino solo artist and was performed almost entirely in Spanish. Part of the field became a sugarcane plantation. Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin were among the guests, and Bad Bunny used the slot to celebrate Puerto Rico.Audience estimates sit around 125 million, per the Television Academy. Other counts put it at 128.2 million. Either way, it was huge. The show later won seven Creative Arts Emmys, the most for any halftime production.2027: Why Jay-Z headlining is differentJay-Z has spent years choosing other people. His company has produced these shows since 2019. Commissioner Roger Goodell has said he asked Jay-Z early on to perform one day, when the timing felt right to him. Jay-Z summed up the arc in his statement, saying "this has been a journey."Hamish Hamilton is reported to direct, and nothing about guests is confirmed. Speculation about Beyoncé is only that. The setting is worth noting, though. SoFi Stadium is the same venue as the 2022 hip-hop show, and the date is Valentine's Day.What the eight shows say about where halftime is goingLook at the list again and a pattern shows up. The shows that landed hardest were the most specific. Lopez and Shakira leaned into Latin identity. Dre's crew was pure Los Angeles. Lamar was personal, and Bad Bunny was proudly Puerto Rican. The NFL used to chase broad, safe nostalgia. Lately it has backed artists with a clear point of view, and the audience numbers followed.Jay-Z fits that mold. His catalogue, from "99 Problems" to "Empire State of Mind," is built on a single city and a single voice. The open question is whether a producer who curated the stage this long will hand the spotlight to a guest, or keep it for himself.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dak Prescott Hypes Cowboys OL With T-Shirt in Trending Photo After Win vs. Eagles
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott complimented the play of his offensive line following Monday night's 38-21 road win over the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott complimented the play of his offensive line following Monday night's 38-21 road win over the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles.

During a postgame interview, Prescott talked up his O-line and wore a shirt that read, "Linemen lead the way."

Prescott's offensive line did not allow a sack against the Eagles' talented defense, which set the stage for the veteran signal-caller to complete 15 of his 27 passing attempts for 212 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions.

Additionally, the linemen paved the way for the Cowboys to rush for 205 yards as a team, spearheaded by Javonte Williams' 155 yards and one touchdown.

Monday's win was a huge one for the Cowboys, as it moved them into sole possession of second place in the NFC East, 1.5 games behind the division-leading New York Giants.

articles.title: 'Eagles Suck,' Cowboys' CeeDee Lamb Talks Motivation After Win in Rivalry Game, 'I Hate Philly'
articles.summary: It wasn't hard for Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb to psych himself up for Monday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
It wasn't hard for Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb to psych himself up for Monday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Appearing on SportsCenter with Scott Van Pelt after the Cowboys' 38-21 victory over their NFC East rivals, Lamb explained he felt like it was going to be a good night because "I hate Philly" and echoed chants from a few Dallas fans in the stands at Lincoln Financial Field saying "Eagles suck."

"Overall, it was just, I don't like losing. I don't do well with losing," Lamb added. "I hate losing more than I like winning. ... It don't sit well with me. I don't have a great day. It ruins my week, and it makes me wanna be a better player, better brother and overall a better man just for my guys because I know how much work we put in each and every week for us to come out and play not how we should. It's a little difficult on my end, so coming out here being very affirmative with how I feel this week."

There was a moment when it looked like the Cowboys were going to have issues against another backup quarterback two weeks after losing to Jalon Daniels and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Philadelphia led 14-10 midway through the second quarter. After the Cowboys scored 10 straight points to go up 20-14, the Eagles responded in the third quarter on Makai Lemon's first career touchdown reception.

It was all Cowboys from that point on. They scored points on three of their next four possessions, including a 16-yard touchdown catch from Lamb that put Dallas up 28-21.

Lamb finished with 74 yards and two touchdowns on five receptions. The Cowboys set season-highs in points and total yards (416) against Philadelphia's defense.

The win snaps Dallas' two-game losing streak and improves the team's record to 3-4. The Cowboys are two games back in the loss column of the New York Giants (4-2-1) for first place in the NFC East.

Dallas' schedule does line up to go on a run before its Week 14 bye week. Four of its next six games are against the Arizona Cardinals, Indianapolis Colts, Tennessee Titans and a rematch with the Eagles.

The two tough tests during that stretch will be in Week 10 against the San Francisco 49ers and Week 13 against the Seattle Seahawks.

articles.title: Travis Kelce vs Patrick Mahomes: How the Chiefs stars built their multimillion-dollar property portfolios in Ohio, Kansas and Missouri
articles.summary: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes work side by side at Arrowhead, but their real estate looks very different.
articles.body: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes work side by side at Arrowhead, but their real estate looks very different. Kelce has spread roughly $12 million across three states: a $995,000 home in Kansas City, a $6 million mansion in Leawood, Kansas, and a $5.35 million lakefront estate in Bratenahl, Ohio, bought in March 2026. Mahomes has gone deep instead of wide. He built a custom estate in Belton, Missouri, and owns a Texas house. Here is how the two portfolios compare, and what the numbers can't tell you.Travis Kelce vs Patrick Mahomes: Who has the bigger property portfolio?On paper, Travis Kelce owns more houses and has spent more on them. Add up his three reported purchases and you land near $12.3 million. When the New York Post ran the numbers in early 2023, Mahomes held an $8 million portfolio across four properties, three of them in Missouri. His Belton estate alone is now pegged at $8 million or more by home-tour sites.That comparison needs a warning label. A purchase price is not a market value, and celebrity home figures often come from listings, county records and educated guesses rather than official statements. Still, the shape of each portfolio is clear. Kelce collects addresses in different places. Mahomes puts his money into one place and builds it up.Geography backs that up. Kelce is the only one with reported property in Missouri, Kansas and Ohio. Nothing public ties Mahomes to Kansas or Ohio. His footprint is Missouri, plus one stop in Texas, the state he grew up in.How Travis Kelce built a three-state map?The first piece arrived in 2019. Realtor.com described a 4,200-square-foot house in Kansas City's Briarcliff West neighborhood, bought for $995,000. One report says he still owns it, though it is no longer his main home.The big move came in late 2023. Kelce paid about $6 million for a gated estate in Leawood, Kansas. It covers roughly 17,000 square feet on just over three acres, beside Hallbrook Country Club. County records listed the buyer as an LLC based in Rocky River, Ohio.The grounds read like a weekend camp. Reports mention a pool, lit pickleball and tennis courts and a mini golf course, plus a theater, wine cellar and gym. The house sits in Tomahawk Creek Estates, a development with only 14 estates, so privacy comes built in. It also gained fame as an address, since Kelce reportedly proposed to Taylor Swift in the backyard.The Ohio mansion that brings Travis Kelce closer to homeThe newest purchase feels the most personal. Kelce grew up in Cleveland Heights, and in 2026 he bought a $5.35 million lakefront mansion in Bratenahl. The Wall Street Journal reported the sale on September 1, and the deal reportedly set a record for Bratenahl.The house dates to 1895 and has about 21,240 square feet on 3.5 acres overlooking Lake Erie. It has eight bedrooms, eight and a half bathrooms, a media room, a spa, a resort-style pool and a five-car garage. Figurati Construction Group bought it in 2023 for $1.95 million, renovated it and sold it on to Kelce. Local reports say the ballroom once hid a speakeasy during Prohibition.Kelce married Swift on July 3 in New York City, a few months after closing on the Ohio house. Reports say the couple is also house-hunting in New York, so Bratenahl may end up as a retreat rather than a base.Why Patrick Mahomes keeps building in one corner of Missouri?Mahomes started small. In December 2017 he paid $350,000 for a Kansas City condo, below the $475,000 asking price. A $1.8 million purchase on West 57th Street followed in January 2019, a 4,300-square-foot house.Then came the 2020 contract extension worth up to $450 million, and a bolder bet. In September that year he bought an eight-acre lot in Belton. Benzinga put the price at roughly $400,000, although some listing sites show a higher figure.Instead of buying a finished mansion, he built one. The estate sits in Loch Lloyd, a gated community about 20 miles south of downtown Kansas City. Reports describe a private football field, a par-3 golf hole, a pool, and a home theater. The $8 million figure is an estimate, not an appraisal.Mahomes also kept a link to home. Around the start of the pandemic, he bought an 8,000-square-foot house in Westlake, Texas, for $3.4 million.What the two strategies say about the players?Kelce's purchases track his life. A first real house as a rising tight end came in 2019. A private fortress arrived once his fame grew. A hometown mansion followed when he became a husband. Each deal added a new state and a new chapter.Mahomes' map is tighter because his life is tighter. He is the franchise quarterback, he has young children, and his backyard doubles as a practice field. Keeping home and work within a short drive makes sense for that job.One gap is worth stating plainly. Neither player has shared rental income, appreciation or returns, so calling these houses investments is partly guesswork. They are also places to live, host and hide. The next entry may land in New York, where Kelce is reportedly searching, while no new Mahomes purchase has surfaced in recent coverage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jones a trade deadline buyer, respect Lurie, Texans D mess, Ravens COY flub, reason JD Vance right on Bengals
articles.summary: Jerry Jones vows the Dallas Cowboys will be active buyers at the NFL trade deadline, seeking roster help for a 3-4 team eyeing the NFC East.
articles.body: Days before the Dallas Cowboys broke a two-game losing skid against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, team owner Jerry Jones stood in a New York City hotel lobby and spoke about playing better and making the team better. "Not only do I have expectations," Jones said of his high hopes for the remainder of the season, "I have really sound basis of saying, we're better than [what we've shown], and we can improve in the areas that have really frustrated us, especially last week." The Cowboys find themselves at 3-4 and within sight of the NFC East-leading New York Giants. COWBOYS, DAK PRESCOTT GET BACK ON TRACK AT THE EXPENSE OF REELING EAGLES IN KEY NFC EAST WIN And Jones is going to spend the next two weeks until the NFL trade deadline trying to add help. "Yeah, I don't have a specific," Jones said. "But I'll be real clear: I would be active if we could get a chance to help the team this year." The trade deadline is 4 p.m. on Nov. 10. The Cowboys will be buyers. Jeff Lurie an Eagles Hall of Famer and national leader Philadelphia Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie was inducted into the Eagles Hall of Fame on Monday and that's logical because the club has won two Super Bowls during his ownership tenure and he is promising more despite the team's struggles this season. "The Eagles Hall of Fame honors those who have made exceptional contributions to the history of this organization and the National Football League," former Eagles quarterback and legend Ron Jaworski said. "Among Jeffrey ’s many qualities, it is his unique ability to lead others that has allowed this team to have sustained success over a long period of time." Let me tell you a different reason Lurie deserves this honor – and your respect. RAVENS PLAYERS RIDE WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP IN MOTORCADE, GET SHOUTOUT DURING SPEECH AT BALTIMORE SHIPYARD EVENT After the Eagles won the Super Bowl in February of 2025, there was considerable pressure on Lurie to turn down an invitation to visit the White House. Although he has in the past donated to politicians of both parties, most people understand Lurie is primarily associated with the Democratic Party. But against that backdrop, the Eagles visited President Donald Trump in April 2025 to celebrate their Super Bowl victory. If Lurie hadn't approved the trip, it would not have happened. But Lurie did what was right in honoring the highest office of the land, regardless of his personal views, and provided everyone a snapshot of national solidarity on behalf of his franchise and the NFL. Others have fallen short of that mark. The White House contacted the Seattle Seahawks about a similar visit this year. But, nothing. The Seahawks officially say they never heard from the White House. They absolutely got an invite via back channels and declined, but rather than paint it as a snub, the White House dropped the issue. The New York Knicks were invited to the White House and club owner James Dolan, a 30-year Trump friend, immediately accepted. And yet, nothing has moved forward. Lurie's decision benefitted the NFL and showed unity to the country by respecting the office of the President – even if he might not have necessarily agreed with the office's occupant. That is leadership. JD VANCE SEES BENGALS MAKING 'A RUN' BUT THAT'S UNDERSTANDABLE BECAUSE HE'S A FAN, ESPECIALLY OF JA'MARR CHASE VP Vance might be right about his Bengals Vice President JD Vance told everyone he thinks the Bengals are about to make a playoff push following their victory over the Baltimore Ravens and, of course, everyone figures Joe Burrow will have to lead that charge if it's going to happen. Maybe. But not completely. The Bengals have gotten Dexter Lawrence to dominate on their defensive line for that run and his impact makes Vance's prediction plausible. The Giants never wanted to move on from Lawrence in the offseason. But when he got ornery that defensive line coach and mentor Andre Patterson was not retained on John Harbaugh's new staff, and became frustrated with his contract status, and didn't show up to the offseason program, and gained weight beyond his enormous 350 pounds, the Giants sent Lawrence to the Bengals for the No. 10 overall selection in last April's draft. Great move so far the Bengals. Lawrence has four sacks from his interior defensive line spot and has seven tackles for loss. He was gobbling burgers in the offseason but is eating up double-team blocks inseason. The Ravens on Sunday managed only 3.1 yards per carry against the Bengals. Derrick Henry rushed for only 45 yards on 17 carries. That happened against a Bengals defense that was the NFL's worst run defense last season. They are No. 19 against the run this season and if Lawrence can lead that continued improvement, Vance is going to be proven correct. NFL's most disappointing unit You can argue which team has been the most disappointing so far this season – the Colts, the Chargers, the Saints, the Rams – and that can change week to week. But the most disappointing unit in the NFL has not changed since Week 1: The Houston Texans defense. That unit opened the season yielding 36 points to the Bills and has since given up 31 points in a game twice and 27 points to the New York Giants on Sunday despite facing J.J. McCarthy in his first start for a team he joined 27 days ago. That performance came despite the fact DeMeco Ryans took over the defensive play-calling a couple of games ago without much improvement to show for it. "Honestly, not to boil this down to simplicity, it comes back to basic fundamentals and techniques," general manager Nick Caserio said. "Tackling is tackling. You're either a good tackler or you're not. We can do some things relative to hidden yardage in some of the areas. "But one of the worst penalized teams in the league, one of the worst tackling teams in the league." The Texans are 20th in the NFL in fewest points allowed per game. That's bottom-third in the league for a unit that was second in the NFL in fewest points allowed last season. The Texans have lost four games this season – against Buffalo, Dallas, Indy and the Giants – on the last possession. On defense. "We put ourselves in a position to win those games," Caserio said. "We just haven't really in the end executed and made enough plays to win." Quickies: Daniel Jones, Steve Bisciotti, undefeated Vikings The Vikings: They're the NFL's only remaining unbeaten team but they're not the NFL's best team by any stretch (the Bills would like a word) and it says here the Perfect Season Miami Dolphins have nothing to worry about. The next month brings games against the Lions, Bills, Packers and 49ers. The Vikings have a great defense, but have scored only five touchdowns in their last five games. Not. Sustainable. Steve Bisciotti: The Ravens have lost consecutive games and their fans think it's all because of Lamar Jackson's absence, but we train the microscope on the club's owner who fired John Harbaugh and most of his staff, including offensive coordinator Todd Monken. Harbaugh with the Giants and Monken with the Browns are both Coach of the Year candidates right now. Myles Garrett: Tick tock, sir. The NFL season has begun. It is time to join the fun and the Rams are optimistic it starts this week. Daniel Jones: Barring a major and unexpected individual rally, he is playing his last season with the Colts. He is signed through next season but the Colts can save $11.6 million in cap space on a pre-June 1 release next offseason or $38 million in cap space on a post-June 1 release. Does the next Colts GM take one of those cap savings options or keep an inconsistent QB who hasn't lived up to his current $88 million contract? Bye, Daniel. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Non-NFL Thought of the Week As a Miami resident I was compelled to root for LeBron James when he played for the Heat years ago, but it was hard because he is unlikable for countless reasons that include he's not a clutch player. That was over a decade ago when he was still good. Now? The only thing that keeps James relevant on the national stage is the ghost of his past abilities and his political antics that make him newsworthy when he does things like practice his golf swing during the national anthem. LeBygone is today nothing more than the NBA's 69th leading scorer, 42nd leading rebounder, an old man who has already missed one of his team's first four games because of back soreness, and the owner of the league's 102nd best field goal percentage. articles.title: “He was screaming and hollering": Keeta Vaccaro’s mother reveals disturbing details during Tyreek Hill’s divorce trial
articles.summary: The divorce battle between Tyreek Hill and Keeta Vaccaro has taken another dramatic turn, with testimony from Vaccaro’s mother bringing a family
articles.body: The divorce battle between Tyreek Hill and Keeta Vaccaro has taken another dramatic turn, with testimony from Vaccaro’s mother bringing a family perspective to the allegations against the former Miami Dolphins star. Alicia Vaccaro told jurors she did not personally see Hill strike her daughter, but described a frightening confrontation that left her concerned for her daughter and newborn grandchild. Her account, alongside testimony from mental health professionals, has added another layer to the ongoing legal dispute, where allegations of domestic violence and emotional distress remain central to the case.Keeta Vaccaro’s mother describes confrontation during Tyreek Hill divorce trialAlicia Vaccaro took the witness stand in Miami on October 8, describing an incident involving Hill and her daughter that prompted her to intervene. She testified that she became alarmed when the argument escalated and Hill appeared determined to get their baby.Recalling the moment, she told the court, “I walked outside the door, and he was pressed up against her. I went toward them. He pushed me back,” Alicia Vaccaro said. “He was screaming, hollering, saying bad words, and then he was gonna go and get the baby. My first instinct was to protect the baby.”She said she and Keeta then entered the room where the baby was and asked Hill not to hurt the child.Jurors also heard audio from a baby monitor recording that captured Hill and Keeta arguing loudly, with banging sounds in the background. The media was not permitted to record the video. According to the testimony, the couple’s newborn was asleep during the confrontation.During cross-examination, Alicia acknowledged that she had not personally witnessed Hill hit or punch her daughter. However, she maintained that the incident shaped her concerns about the couple’s relationship.Keeta has previously described alleged physical confrontations, including an incident in which she claimed Hill pushed her onto a bed and threw objects around a room. Hill has denied the allegations.Mental health experts testify about Keeta Vaccaro’s allegationsThe trial also featured testimony from forensic psychologist Dr. Sheila Rapa, who evaluated Keeta and said she diagnosed her with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).Rapa discussed symptoms including dissociation and heightened awareness of Hill’s moods. She also addressed why someone might remain in an unhealthy relationship, suggesting that emotional attachment and lifestyle factors could play a role.“Yes, I think that comes with the lifestyle,” Rapa testified when asked whether financial circumstances and the lifestyle associated with the relationship could influence someone’s attachment.Hill’s attorneys challenged Rapa’s expertise and stressed that she was a hired expert, not Keeta’s treating physician. Rapa confirmed she had been paid nearly $6,000 for her involvement in the case.Therapist Dr. Jennifer Wilson separately testified that Keeta arrived for treatment with a PTSD diagnosis and experienced sleep difficulties, racing thoughts and problems concentrating.Keeta’s brother, Kevin Vaccaro, also described concerns about changes in his sister and recalled hearing her scream during a phone call when Hill was allegedly yelling in the background.Keeta is seeking monetary damages through claims that include battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress. articles.title: Dak Prescott Says Cowboys' NFC East Title Hopes Are 'Right in Front of Us' After Win vs. Eagles
articles.summary: Despite a rough start to the season for the Dallas Cowboys, Dak Prescott is feeling optimistic about their chances in the NFC East after a 38-21 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.
articles.body:
Despite a rough start to the season for the Dallas Cowboys, Dak Prescott is feeling optimistic about their chances in the NFC East after a 38-21 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.

Speaking to reporters following the Cowboys' win, Prescott said their hopes for an NFC East title are "right in front of us" if they keep taking care of business:

"We say the division's right in front of us. It is as long as we win. And if you lose another game, then you're probably checking to see what New York's doing. You're probably checking and watching the other teams more than we should. So yeah, I mean you got to win games, got to win division games. How big of a game this was, understanding how much they're hurt on their offensive side, yeah, huge road win for us."

The Cowboys' formula for success this season was supposed to be a dominant offense and an improved defense that might not be among the NFL's elite, but wouldn't be at the bottom in several categories like it was in 2025.

That hadn't panned out through the first six games. The offense had been inconsistent, including scoring 29 points in their previous two games combined, and the defense was still getting picked apart.

Monday night is hard to gauge as a litmus test because the Eagles are so beat up right now, but the Cowboys winning as impressively as they did is what a team with playoff aspirations should do against an inferior opponent.

The Cowboys set season-highs in points scored, total yards (416) and rushing yards (204).

This victory was significant because it snapped Dallas' two-game losing streak and gave the team 2-1 against the NFC East. The lone defeat was in Week 1 against the Giants, who are currently in first place and riding high after J.J. McCarthy led a win over the Houston Texans.

New York (4-2-1) is two games up on the Cowboys with a head-to-head victory already in the bank. The two teams have six common opponents remaining, including the Jacksonville Jaguars, San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks.

That doesn't include the second matchup between the Giants and Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Week 17.

Dallas is set up to potentially make a move after defeating the Eagles because its next two games are home against the Arizona Cardinals and at the Indianapolis Colts.

The Giants are on a bye in Week 8 before back-to-back divisional games against the Eagles and Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley Injured, Latest on Eagles Star's Status vs. Commanders After Exit vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley provided a positive update after leaving Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys during the third quarter.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley provided a positive update after leaving Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys during the third quarter.

Barkley, who missed the Eagles' previous two games with a hamstring injury, told reporters that he hurt his back on a 29-yard run in the first quarter while trying to "compensate" for the hamstring ailment:

However, Barkley told reporters that "his hamstring came out great," and added that he doesn't anticipate missing any time with the back injury.

The 2-5 Eagles will be back in action Sunday night when they go on the road to face the NFC East rival Washington Commanders.

Per ESPN's Tim McManus , Barkley played only nine offensive snaps on Monday, but he touched the ball on all of them, finishing with 62 rushing yards and a touchdown on seven carries, plus two receptions for nine yards.

Barkley appeared to be in discomfort following a five-yard run late in the third quarter, as he was hunched over and wincing on the sidelines.

The 29-year-old veteran did not return to the game after that, as the rushing burden largely fell on the shoulders of Dameon Pierce from that point forward.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Barkley discussed the difficulty of playing through injuries due to the desire to help his team win.

"It's kind of the school of thought I come from: I truly love this game, and I feel like if you're able to go, sometimes you've got to push your body to the limit," Barkley said. "I'm trying, it's just not responding the way I want it to respond right now. It sucks because I'm trying to be the best leader I can be, and it's hard when you're not able to be out there and perform for your team."

Philly took a 21-20 lead during the third quarter, but it was all Dallas from there, as the Cowboys scored 18 unanswered points to close out the game.

Given Barkley's limitations, the absence of wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, and the fact that quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season, the Tanner McKee-led offense put forth a valiant effort on Monday night.

The Eagles accrued 321 yards of total offense and converted 23 first downs without several of their most important offensive players.

While Smith and Wicks will be back at some point, and Barkley's comments suggest he intends to play next week against the Commanders, the Eagles have no choice other than to move forward with their backup quarterback in McKee.

That makes having a healthy and effective Barkley even more paramount, but with the injuries continuing to mount, it is fair to wonder if he will be limited moving forward.

The 2026 NFL trade deadline could bring about some surprising deals that completely shift the league's landscape.

While pro football's trade deadline used to be relatively quiet compared to other sports, things have changed in recent years. The leadup to the 2025 deadline saw over a dozen deals go down, including several first-round picks and superstars changing hands.

Plenty more exciting trades could be in store with approximately a third of the league having two or fewer wins going into Week 8.

With that in mind, here's a look at five potential shock trades that could occur at the 2026 trade deadline.

Buffalo Bills Fix Secondary with Budda Baker

Arizona Cardinals receive: 2027 third-round draft pick

The Bills made some sweeping changes this offseason after coming up painfully short of a Super Bowl yet again in the Josh Allen era. While many of these adjustments have been successful based on the team's hot start, the secondary has become a liability and could be an Achilles' heel if it isn't addressed at the trade deadline.

The Bills have jumped out to a 5-1 record despite a sieve-like pass defense that has allowed an eye-popping 285.8 yards per game. Only the Detroit Lions have given up more passing yardage in 2026. Buffalo also ranks 30th in scoring defense and has allowed 15 passing touchdowns, tied for the third-most in the league.

While the Bills reinforced the cornerback position by bringing Tre'Davious White back into the fold for the third time, adding a versatile safety like Budda Baker could be what leads this secondary back to respectability.

Baker has been languishing on a Cardinals team that has only reached the playoffs once during his nine-plus seasons with the club. The eight-time Pro Bowler has been one of the few consistent bright spots in recent years and remains a force despite Arizona's dismal 2-5 start to the 2026 campaign.

Although he's in an age-30 season, Baker still has plenty to offer a Super Bowl contender. In seven games this season, he's already recorded a career-best 3.5 sacks while also contributing 44 tackles, four pass defenses and an interception. He's also under contract through next season after agreeing to a three-year, $54 million extension in December 2024.

Given his versatility, high football IQ and ability to cover, support the run and attack the quarterback with equal skill, Baker would be the optimal defensive back for the Bills to make a run at leading up to the trade deadline. He can slot in at either safety position, instantly upgrading a Buffalo defense that sorely needs a playmaker of Baker's caliber.

Detroit Lions Address Secondary with Donte Jackson

Los Angeles Chargers receive: 2027 sixth-round draft pick

The Detroit Lions were expected to return to prominence after a disappointing 2025 season ended without a playoff berth, but the team is being plagued by many of the same issues in 2026.

One of the most glaring problems in the Motor City is the defense, specifically a passing defense that has given up a league-worst 291.8 yards per game and the second-most touchdowns through the air (16).

While Detroit is tied for the most sacks in the league with 21 and is getting reliable pressure thanks to Aidan Hutchinson and DJ Wonnum, the secondary has been a disaster. The cornerback room is desperate for an upgrade, one that will likely need to come via the trade market to have the type of impact required for real change.

Jackson should be available after the Chargers fell completely out of contention before the calendar flipped to November. Considering the team remains winless going into Week 8, it would be a surprise if the Bolts don't host a fire sale that sees several veterans on expiring contracts, including Jackson, shipped off for draft capital.

Although Jackson isn't a perennial Pro Bowler, he's the type of reliable, steady defensive back with nearly a decade of starting experience who could help transform a secondary. He's played in 116 games for three different franchises since entering the league as a second-round pick in the 2018 draft. He had one of his better coverage seasons in 2025—his first with the Chargers—allowing completions on just 21 of 49 targets for 287 yards and three touchdowns.

If Detroit does land Jackson, the corner profiles as a starter on the outside across from D.J. Reed. That upgrade could be all it takes to get this defense on the right track and have it playing far better in the second half of the campaign.

Minnesota Vikings Jump-Start the Offense with Saquon Barkley

Minnesota Vikings receive: RB Saquon Barkley

Philadelphia Eagles receive: 2027 third- and sixth-round draft picks

With the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers both faltering in Week 7, the Vikings stand alone as the NFL's last remaining undefeated team. It's apparent that this team has the potential to make a Super Bowl run, but the offense hasn't played nearly up to the level of excellence the team's defense has established.

One way to jump-start a unit that has been averaging a pitiful 281.7 yards per game (the fourth-fewest in football) is to acquire a game-changing running back. Saquon Barkley could be available for the right price after the Eagles dropped their fifth consecutive game on Monday night.

Barkley may not be the same player that rushed for over 2,000 yards and carried Philadelphia to a Lombardi Trophy two years ago, but he's still a highly effective, versatile lead back who would add a new dimension to an offense that has grown stagnant.

Despite missing two games with injury and playing behind a depleted offensive line that has lost multiple starters, Barkley has still managed to tally 244 rushing yards and a touchdown on 43 totes—averaging a strong 5.7 yards per carry. He hasn't been contributing much as a pass-catcher in 2026 (hauling in six of nine targets for 17 yards), but has proven in years past that he can easily impact a game as a receiver when called upon.

While Minnesota isn't desperate for running back help right now, it wouldn't be wise to count on a 31-year-old Aaron Jones to stay healthy on his current 300-plus carry pace. Backup Jordan Mason has already missed several games with injury and hasn't moved the needle much when he has been available.

Adding Barkley is the type of forward-thinking maneuver championship hopefuls make at the deadline. By the time he's up to speed and fully integrated into head coach Kevin O'Connell's system, he'll be ready to supercharge Minnesota's offense and shoulder a heavy load throughout a potential deep playoff run.

Garrett Wilson Revives Struggling San Francisco 49ers' Receiving Corps

San Francisco 49ers receive: WR Garrett Wilson

New York Jets receive: 2027 first- and fourth-round draft picks

The San Francisco 49ers remain a Super Bowl favorite despite their disappointing 29-20 defeat to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. The team's first defeat of 2026 did highlight some roster inadequacies, though, with the most notable being at the wide receiver position.

San Francisco's receiving corps has dealt with a slew of injuries this year, with the issue coming to a head over the weekend when San Francisco was forced to rely on the likes of Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks to serve as Brock Purdy's top receiving options.

Wilson would be a landscape-shifting acquisition, a star in his prime who could serve as San Francisco's top receiver not only for the remainder of the 2026 campaign but also the foreseeable future. He inked a four-year, $130 million extension in July 2025, a deal that will keep him under contract through the 2030 season.

While Wilson has struggled with consistency this year, he's still managed to reel in 37 of his 51 targets for 444 receiving yards and three touchdowns—keeping him on pace for his fourth 1,000-yard receiving campaign in his first five NFL seasons. He's accomplishing this despite being saddled with a low-end starting quarterback in Geno Smith and an offense that only averages a shade over 200 passing yards per game.

Wilson could be rejuvenated in the Bay Area, working with one of the league's top passers in Purdy. Mike Evans and Wilson would give San Francisco a truly elite receiving tandem to chase a ring with this year, while the latter could eventually take over as the club's main WR1 as the 33-year-old Evans approaches the latter stages of his career.

It won't be easy to pry Wilson away from Gang Green, but the recent rise of rookie Omar Cooper Jr. may help convince the 2-5 Jets to move on at the deadline in exchange for several premium picks.

Jonathan Taylor Bolsters Seattle Seahawks' Title Defense

Seattle Seahawks receive: RB Jonathan Taylor

Indianapolis Colts receive: RB Emmanuel Wilson, 2027 second- and fourth-round picks

The Seattle Seahawks' title defense hit a snag when the team lost three of four games between Weeks 3-6, but the squad started trending the right direction again with a big win over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs this week.

Seattle still doesn't look like a strong candidate to join the Chiefs and New England Patriots as the only repeat champs since the turn of the millennium, however, and shouldn't hesitate to make a blockbuster move at the deadline to improve its odds.

Acquiring Jonathan Taylor would push Seattle's offense back to the league's upper echelon and allow the club to follow the same blueprint it did during last year's Lombardi Trophy run.

Seattle leaned heavily on Kenneth Walker III to carry the offense during the playoffs, but lost the Super Bowl MVP in free agency. The team attempted to draft a replacement in Jadarian Price, but thus far the first-round rookie has underwhelmed and dealt with significant injuries.

Emmanuel Wilson has helped plug the hole while Zach Charbonnet continues to work his way back from an ACL tear, but trading for Taylor would give the team an established lead back to run the offense around for the long haul.

Taylor has been one of the few effective players on a dismal Colts team. He's turned 140 totes into 587 rushing yards and a league-leading eight touchdowns while adding 178 receiving yards on 17 receptions. Despite his best efforts, Indy dropped to 2-5 this weekend and remains well out of contention.

Bringing Taylor into the mix would significantly elevate a Seahawks ground attack that is averaging a middling 113.7 yards per game right now. That is nearly 10 yards below what the team rushed for during the 2025 campaign and almost 20 yards fewer than it averaged during its three-game postseason run.

While the move would cost the Seahawks some premium picks, upgrading Wilson to Taylor would have a transformative effect—catapulting Seattle back near the top of the Super Bowl favorites list.

articles.summary: Week 7 was another wild one in the NFL, with two of the league's last undefeated teams suffering their first losses. Week 8 figures to bring more of the same, and it should carry a fair bit of uncertainty for fantasy managers, too.
articles.body:
Week 7 was another wild one in the NFL, with two of the league's last undefeated teams suffering their first losses. Week 8 figures to bring more of the same, and it should carry a fair bit of uncertainty for fantasy managers, too.

Injuries continue to impact the fantasy football landscape, and some legitimate fantasy stars will be on bye this week. The Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants, and San Francisco 49ers will have the week off.

Here, you'll find early point-per-reception (PPR) rankings for the top plays of Week 8, along with some high-upside sleepers who may still be available on the waiver wire.

The Miami Dolphins got their first win of 2026 on Sunday, thanks to a strong dual-threat effort by quarterback Malik Willis.

Having rookie receiver Caleb Douglas in the lineup certainly helped, as he caught a pair of touchdown passes against the New York Jets. Willis, meanwhile, threw for 208 yards, rushed for 37 yards and a score, and finished with 26 fantasy points.

The New England Patriots will provide a stiffer test this week, as they've allowed an average of just 15.7 fantasy points to opposing QBs. However, Willis' scrambling ability should provide a reasonable floor, and he's rostered in only 20 percent of fantasy leagues.

Sleeper: Zonovan Knight, Arizona Cardinals

To be fair, Zonovan Knight's sleeper hinges heavily on the availability of rookie running back Jeremiyah Love. However, Knight has emerged as the top back, over Tyler Allgeier, with Love out.

Knight rushed for 48 yards and 6.9 yards per carry against the Denver Broncos on Sunday, and he added 15 yards on three receptions. He'll have a much more favorable matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Dallas' defense has been a liability all season, especially against the run. The Cowboys entered Monday night surrendering an average of 18.3 fantasy points to opposing running backs.

Knight is rostered in only 14 percent of fantasy leagues.

After topping 22 fantasy points in consecutive weeks, Jets rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. figures to be one of the top waiver-wire adds ahead of Week 8. The Indiana product has established himself as the clear-cut second option opposite Garrett Wilson, and he may have even taken over the No. 1 role.

Cooper has rapidly become one of Geno Smith's favorite options. He saw five targets in Week 7, while Wilson only saw three.

This week, Cooper will have a solid matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, who have surrendered an average of 26.6 fantasy points to opposing receiver groups. That's a middle-of-the-pack ranking, but Cooper's target share gives him tremendous upside.

Cooper is still only rostered in 39 percent of fantasy leagues.

Sleeper: Brenton Strange, Jacksonville Jaguars

The Jacksonville Jaguars are coming off their bye and will look to get back on track against the rival Indianapolis Colts. Tight end Brenton Strange should be a big part of their offensive game plan.

Strange has seen at least seven targets in each of his past three outings. He logged 9.4 fantasy points in Week 6 and reached double digits in both Week 4 and Week 5. He should approach double digits again with Indy coming to town.

The Colts have surrendered an average of 11.3 fantasy points to opposing tight ends. Strange is rostered in 46 percent of fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Kaepernick, diez años después de arrodillarse durante el himno de EE.UU: "Lo volvería a hacer"
articles.standfirst: El gesto de protesta racial le valió a ex quaterback de los San Francisco 49ers el final de su carrera. Desde 2017 no ha sido contratado por ninguna franquicia de la NFL
articles.summary: El gesto de protesta racial le valió a ex quaterback de los San Francisco 49ers el final de su carrera. Desde 2017 no ha sido contratado por ninguna franquicia de la NFL
articles.body: Su gesto dio la vuelta al mundo en 2016. Colin Kaepernick se arrodilló durante el himno de Estados Unidos en un partido de pretemporada. El ex quaterback de los San Francisco 49ers llevó la protesta racial del 'Black Lives Matter' (La vida de los negros es importante) a la NFL. Era su forma de denunciar la injusticia racial y la brutalidad policial en Estados Unidos. Lo repitió durante 11 partidos. Kaepernick explicó su gesto tras el partido: "No voy a levantarme y mostrar orgullo por la bandera de un país que oprime a la gente negra y de color. Para mí, esto es más importante que el fútbol y sería egoísta por mi parte mirar hacia otro lado". Inspiró a otros jugadores de la NFL a seguir su ejemplo. Pero a raíz de él se generó un debate nacional porque muchos los consideraron una falta de respeto. Uno de los que más críticos fue Donald Trump, entonces candidato a la presidencia de EE.UU. Su carrera dio un vuelco irreversible. En 2017, se convirtió en agente libre y no fue contratado por ningún equipo de la NFL pese a haber llevado a los 49ers al Super Bowl de 2013 y de haber lanzado 16 pases de touchdown en su última temporada. Aquel gesto supuso el final de su carrera deportiva. Fue 'repudiado' por los propietarios de las franquicias al considerar su desplante al himno como algo antipatriótico. Diez años después, Kaepernick ha reconocido en una entrevista a BBC Sport, que no se arrepiente pese al alto precio que tuvo que pagar. "Sabía que la protesta podría costarme mi carrera... Sin duda lo volvería a hacer", asegura. El ex quarterback recuerda así lo sucedido. "Lo que no pude predecir fue la cantidad de gente que me apoyaría de manera significativa, y también la gente que trabajaría en mi contra y en contra del movimiento", añade. Para quienes defienden que el deporte y la política deben mantenerse separados, él lo tiene claro. "Resultan muy hipócritas, porque la política forma parte intrínseca del deporte. Vemos en el fútbol americano que los contribuyentes financian los estadios de la NFL. Vemos a los dueños de los equipos de la NFL apoyando a candidatos políticos... así que intentar presentar esto como si el deporte no fuera político, en muchos sentidos me parece ridículo y ajeno a la realidad", señala en BBC. Considera "lamentable" que la FIFA otorgase a Trump su primer "Premio de la Paz", un presidente que "trata activamente de usar el deporte para ganar favores y popularidad". "Lo que me parece genial es verlo aparecer en estos eventos y que sea abucheado por el público, lo cual refleja el ambiente político que ha creado, con el que la mayoría del país no está de acuerdo... cuando se trata de deportes, la gente debe seguir reaccionando en consecuencia", añade.
