articles.title: Jalen Hurts’ diagnosis renews questions about conflicts in NFL medical care
articles.summary: As questions continue about the medical care Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts received before doctors discovered blood clots in his lungs, NBC Philadelphia found that researchers a decade ago raised broader concerns about potential conflicts of interest in NFL players’ medical care.
articles.body: As questions continue about the medical care Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts received before doctors discovered blood clots in his lungs, NBC Philadelphia found that researchers a decade ago raised broader concerns about potential conflicts of interest in NFL players’ medical care. The Harvard University report recommended separating the medical professionals responsible for treating players from those responsible for evaluating players for their teams. The NFL Players Association, the union representing NFL players, funded the 2016 study through a grant. Hurts is likely out for the rest of the season after doctors found blood clots in his lungs and leg. The discovery came after the Eagles traveled to England, where doctors cleared Hurts to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars after finding a superficial blood clot in his calf. After Hurts returned home, doctors learned that blood clots had traveled to his lungs, the team said. Because of medical privacy laws, the public may never learn everything about Hurts’ treatment. Last week, the NFLPA called for an investigation into what led to Hurts’ diagnosis and why he was allowed to play after doctors found a clot in his leg. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he would welcome a review, and over the weekend, both the league and the union said they were jointly examining how Hurts’ diagnosis was handled. There is no indication at this point that the potential conflict identified by Harvard researchers played any role in Hurts’ medical care. But his case comes as the NFL faces renewed scrutiny over a question researchers examined years ago: Can medical professionals adequately serve the interests of both the player and the team? “There is no doctor who is taking orders from a football person, a non-medical person, period,” NFL Chief Medical Officer Dr. Allen Sills told reporters during a news conference last week. Under the current collective bargaining agreement between the NFL and NFLPA, teams retain medical personnel to care for players. The agreement states that “the club medical personnel’s primary duty in providing player medical care shall be not to the Club but instead to the player-patient,” regardless of the fact that the club retains the medical professional or their hospital, clinic or medical group. In 2016, Harvard researchers studying the health and well-being of current and former NFL players identified what they called an “inherent conflict of interest” in the responsibilities club medical staff have to both players and their teams. “The foremost obvious duty they have is to treat players, but then they also have a duty to advise teams about players’ health, both in the short term and long term,” sports attorney Chris Deubert, who co-authored the Harvard study, said. The researchers proposed separating those responsibilities. Under their recommendation, one group would be responsible for player care and treatment. A separate club doctor would evaluate players for the club’s business purposes. “It doesn’t mean that the players don’t get excellent health care the vast majority of the time or even all of the time,” Deubert said. “But it does erode the level of trust between players and the medical staff.” An NFL spokesperson criticized the study as dated and disputed its findings. “It was inaccurate then, and it’s inaccurate today,” the spokesperson said. Sills also rejected the suggestion that team officials influence medical decisions. “Any idea or any suggestion that a team physician is ever being influenced by a coach, a general manager, a team owner, it just doesn’t happen,” Sills said. Dr. Aaron Baggish, a former team cardiologist for the New England Patriots who stopped working with the organization in 2022 and is now involved with NFL research at Harvard, described the competing responsibilities differently. “There’s always inherent conflict,” Baggish said. “They have an obligation to address the needs and the demands of their employer, which is typically the general management and the coaching staff. And at the same time, they have a medical and ethical responsibility to do what’s right by the athletes.” NFL players are allowed to obtain a second medical opinion under the collective bargaining agreement. The agreement says a player must consult with the club physician before following a course of treatment recommended by the second-opinion physician. The contract language addressing medical personnel has become more specific since Harvard released its report in 2016. The 2020 contract, updated from the 2011 agreement, applies more broadly to club medical personnel and makes clear that their primary duty when providing medical care is to the player-patient, even though they or their medical organizations are retained by the club. Deubert, however, said the potential structural conflict identified by the researchers remains. “It’s an attack on the structure to raise serious questions about the structure and whether there could be something better and that they have not seriously engaged with,” Deubert said. “I think that’s disappointing.” The NFLPA did not respond to a request for comment. Representatives for the Eagles directed questions to the NFL. It remains unclear whether the investigation sought by the players’ association will examine only the decisions surrounding Hurts’ diagnosis and treatment or whether it will also examine the broader medical structure Harvard researchers scrutinized a decade ago.

articles.title: No voters’ name deleted based on Form 7 In DK
articles.summary: Dakshina Kannada final electoral roll adds 32,061 voters post-SIR; 9,064 removed for valid reasons. No deletions accepted via Form 7 objections.
articles.body: Mangaluru: The final electoral roll of Dakshina Kannada saw an increase of 32,061 voters compared to the draft list. While the draft voters list published on Aug 24 had 16,46,387 names, the final electoral roll published on Tuesday includes 16,78,448 eligible electors. There are 8,23,198 men, 8,55,232 women and 18 third-gender voters in the final voter list.Deputy commissioner Darshan HV told reporters on Tuesday that 9,064 voters were removed, including 87 dead, 7,627 permanently shifted, six already enrolled and 1,384 were marked as ineligible during the hearing. Names of 40 people having citizenship of other countries have also been removed from the final list.Of the 40 voters with foreign citizenship, 17 were from Nepal, two from the UK, five from Canada, six each from Australia and America, and one each from the Netherlands, South Africa, Ireland and Norway. In response to a query, the DC explained that these voters are of Indian origin who acquired citizenship in other countries over time, but their names remained on the voter list.He said Dakshina Kannada issued the highest number of notices for discrepancies in the state. While the district issued notices to 1,50,131 voters, 1,48,739 were considered eligible for the final list after the hearing process.The final voter list has 25,326 young voters in the age group of 18 to 19, while the draft voter list had only 12,418 young voters. Meanwhile, the final list has 14,086 voters aged above 85 years. The district has 366 NRI voters and 449 service voters, he said.All Form 7 applications invalidThe DC said that none of the objections received through Form 7 or without Form 7 were found valid and no voters were deleted based on such requests in the district. The district received 1,205 requests, including 879 through Form 7, registering objections. However, none of them were found valid. As many as 326 objections were filed on a plain sheet of paper without mentioning a name or address. The DC said that not every objection had a malafide intention. articles.summary: Troy Aikman could leave ESPN after the 2026 NFL season, with his contract set to expire and no new deal announced.
articles.body: Troy Aikman could leave ESPN after the 2026 NFL season, with his contract set to expire and no new deal announced. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback has confirmed that he plans to finish the season before exploring his options. Meanwhile, reports of a new ESPN contract for Joe Buck and an alleged disagreement between the longtime partners have added uncertainty to their future on Monday Night Football.Aikman and Buck have worked together for more than two decades, first at Fox and then at ESPN. They are also expected to call Super Bowl LXI on February 14, 2027. Whether they continue working together beyond that game remains an open question. Troy Aikman opens up about his ESPN contract and next moveAikman discussed his future during an appearance on Dallas sports radio station KTCK. He confirmed that he would finish the current NFL season before deciding what comes next.“I’ll broadcast through this season, and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens,” Aikman said during the interview.The 59-year-old analyst also spoke about the Super Bowl and the possibility of finding another broadcasting home. His ESPN contract reportedly pays him around $18 million annually and expires after the 2026 season.Aikman's comments leave the door open to several possibilities. He could negotiate a new deal with ESPN or explore offers from other networks. For now, however, he has not announced plans to leave, and ESPN has not confirmed an extension.His next move could shape the future of Monday Night Football, where he has worked alongside Buck since 2022. The pair joined ESPN after leaving Fox, where they had called NFL games together since 2002. Joe Buck’s new ESPN deal puts their partnership under scrutinyBuck's contract has added to the questions surrounding the broadcast duo. articles.title: NFL Week 8 betting: 5 biggest storylines, including the undefeated Vikings being underdogs
articles.summary: The Vikings travel to face the Lions this week.
articles.body:
Home-field advantage keeps disappearing in the NFL.

After the Dallas Cowboys won Monday night, road teams are 54-52-1 this season, according to Covers.com . The split gets even wider when the spread is involved. Road teams are 62-45 against the spread this season. Home-field advantage has been lessened through the years and through seven weeks this season, it really hasn't mattered at all.

Here are five betting storylines heading into Week 8 of the NFL season:

There's one undefeated team left in the NFL, and they're underdogs in Week 8.

The Minnesota Vikings are 6-0 and travel to face the Detroit Lions. If the Vikings feel like their great start is being disrespected, it won't get better once they see that the Lions are favored by a full field goal. The Vikings are undefeated straight up but not against the spread. They are 4-2 against the spread. Every team in the NFL has at least two losses against the spread this season.

Road teams are doing well against the spread this season and so are underdogs. A surge by underdogs the past few weeks puts them at 58-48 against the spread this season. Road underdogs are a strong 38-25 ATS (60.3%) this season, via Covers.com .

That ATS record should even out as the season goes on, but to this point it has been smart to take the points.

Throwing for 249 yards and four touchdowns in a half, when your team outscores a major division rival 35-0, is going to get some attention. Especially when it's Joe Burrow.

The Cincinnati Bengals have taken over as the betting favorites to win the AFC North, and Burrow is making his move in the MVP race after he went nuclear against the Ravens in the second half on Sunday. Josh Allen is still the big favorite with +140 odds at BetMGM, but Burrow has slid into second place at +450.

Burrow's numbers are exceptional this season and the Bengals are having team success, which gives him a chance. Voters like spreading the award around, which worked in Allen's favor two years ago and could help Burrow this time. Burrow has a very favorable schedule the next few weeks, starting with the Titans in Week 8, so he should continue to cut into Allen's lead.

The Lamar Jackson situation is making life complicated in Baltimore, and for oddsmakers too. The Ravens quarterback remained out last week with an ankle injury and Baltimore got blown out. Cincinnati covered the spread easily. We're probably in for another week of wondering if Jackson will return, which makes it tough to set a line on what is arguably the marquee game of the week.

The Ravens face the Buffalo Bills, and the Bills are 3.5-point favorites. That indicates that oddsmakers expect Jackson back, because a Tyler Huntley-led team wouldn't be that short of an underdog on the road, but the Ravens are still getting more than a field goal. That line could fluctuate a few times this week based on injury updates for Jackson.

The Rams' Super Bowl odds are fascinating. Oddsmakers don't want major exposure on the Rams if they turn it around, so after one good win against the Raiders last week Los Angeles moved back up the Super Bowl odds board. They are tied for fourth in Super Bowl odds at +1100. The only three teams with shorter odds are the 49ers, Bills and Chiefs. That's not a major move considering the Rams were fifth in the odds last week, but it's a trend that should continue.

The Rams have a soft portion of their schedule coming up, so they should improve upon their 3-4 record. And if they do, their odds will continue to get shorter. Their odds don't match the results so far this season, but there simply won't be a time in which the Rams' championship odds present fantastic value.

articles.title: Oregon Quarterback Dante Moore Not Expected to Return This Season Weeks After He Suffered a Brutal Hit to the Head
articles.summary: Moore, 21, was taken to the hospital in an ambulance after suffering a concussion during a game against the USC Trojans in Los Angeles on Sept. 26
articles.body:
University of Oregon quarterback Dante Moore isn't expected back for the rest of the season after suffering a concussion in a game last month

Oregon Ducks coach Dan Lanning said in a press conference that the 21-year-old's return is not his decision despite his desire to play, following a hit on the head in a game against the University of Southern California Trojans in Los Angeles on Sept. 26

Moore has been able to resume practicing, but Lanning explained that featuring him in a game would be riskier because they can't "control the setting" to the same extent

University of Oregon quarterback Dante Moore is expected to miss the rest of the season after suffering a hit to the head in a game last month.

Moore, a highly-rated 2027 NFL Draft prospect, suffered a concussion during the Oregon Ducks' game against the University of Southern California Trojans in Los Angeles on Sept. 26.

Moore, 21, resumed practice earlier this month, but Ducks coach Dan Lanning said he doesn't expect him to return to games this season.

"I'm not anticipating him being back, no," Lanning said during his weekly press conference in Eugene, Ore., on Monday, Oct. 26.

"I think if it was up to Dante, he would want to be out there playing for the guys," he explained. "But unfortunately it's not really up to Dante. It's not really up to me. We can control the setting at practice where he's able to do things for us. That's not always the case in the game."

Moore was injured after sliding during a play in the second quarter of the Sept. 26 game.

Trojans linebacker Desman Stephen II hit him, driving his head into the ground before staff rushed onto the field to treat him. He was placed on a stretcher and then taken into an ambulance.

A fight nearly broke out as Oregon players confronted USC defenders, and officials and coaches tried to break it up. Stephen received a targeting penalty and was disqualified.

Lanning avoided speculation about whether Moore, who transferred to Oregon from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 2024, would return next season.

"We'd love to have Dante out there," he said. "He's still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward, finding opportunities for us to be better. I can tell you, we're getting one of the best scout-team quarterback looks every single week in practice, and he looks good out there," Lanning said.

Moore was named the top college football recruit by Sports Illustrated in 2022, joining the UCLA Bruins from Martin Luther King High School in Detroit the following January as an early enrollee, ESPN reported at the time.

He appeared in nine games for the team before transferring to Oregon, per ESPN . He spent 2024 as backup for Dillon Gabriel, now with the Cleveland Browns, before taking a redshirt.

Last year, he earned third-team All-Big Ten honors, CBS News reported. He could have entered the 2026 NFL Draft, but decided to return to college.

In four games this season, Moore threw for 926 yards and nine touchdowns with no interceptions, per ESPN .

articles.title: Rams have hardest remaining schedule in NFL based on this metric
articles.summary: The Rams' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, so if they're going to make the playoffs, they'll have to earn it.
articles.body:
No one in Los Angeles is satisfied with how the Rams have started the season . They're 3-4 after seven games, grinding through a schedule that had some favorable matchups, as well as some difficult ones.

The playoffs are still well within reach, but if the Rams are going to make the postseason, they're certainly going to earn it.

According to Ben Baldwin, the Rams' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL. That's based on the average remaining opponent win percentage against a league-average team on a neutral field.

The Rams' schedule is clearly the toughest, with an opponent win percentage of more than 55% in such projections, while the Bengals ' is by far the easiest, well below 45%.

Their next three games are all against teams below .500, including the winless Chargers and the 1-4-1 Commanders. In Week 10, they'll have a rematch with the Cardinals , who upset the Rams as 12.5-point underdogs.

After the Week 11 bye, the slate gets incredibly difficult. Only two of their final seven opponents are below .500 right now, and that includes a dangerous Cowboys team and a Buccaneers team that just blew out the Panthers.

The Rams aren't looking ahead to their remaining schedule, but after looking at their final seven opponents, it's abundantly clear just how important these next three games against the Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals are.

Los Angeles almost has to go 3-0 and get to 6-4 before the bye because there are some challenging games awaiting after the break.

articles.title: Steelers linked to exciting trade for first-round WR
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers were just named as a potential trade landing spot for Jacksonville Jaguars Pro Bowl wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.
articles.body:
Trade rumors are flying left and right, and the Pittsburgh Steelers have just been linked to an exciting trade for a former first-round wide receiver who can absolutely change the game thanks to his lightning-fast speed.

While discussing availability rumors surrounding Jacksonville Jaguars Pro Bowl wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr., ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler linked the Steelers and Kansas City Chiefs as trade partners to keep an eye on.

"Brian Thomas Jr., immensely talented, but I've talked to several teams who believe that he could be dealt over the next few weeks," Fowler said. "Jacksonville has relented in the past, they kept him cause he's such a big talent. They hoped his deep threat would balance things out for their other receivers. Last two weeks, no catches, had just 15 snaps and was essentially benched in the London game against Houston. Something has to give. There's going to be some interested parties. Kansas City has looking around about potentially adding a receiver. Pittsburgh to some extent. There will be some suitors for some of these top guys."

Thomas, who was drafted by the Jaguars with the 23rd overall pick in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft, found tremendous success as a rookie, recording 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2024. Unfortunately, his production fell apart in 2025 and to start 2026, accumulating just 812 receiving yards and three touchdowns in the past 20 games.

Taking a backseat role to Jaguars wide receivers Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, Thomas has played less than 60% of snaps in five out of six games this season, including seeing the field on just 21% of snaps in Week 6 and not having caught a pass in his past two games.

With a trade seemingly the most likely outcome and Pittsburgh named as a top landing spot, we at Steelers Wire will monitor this situation with Thomas very carefully over the next several weeks.

articles.title: Dak Prescott Talks 'Hungry, Pissed Off Version' of Cowboys HC Schottenheimer After Win vs. Eagles
articles.summary: After a dominant 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer appeared more subdued than usual.
articles.body:
After a dominant 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer appeared more subdued than usual.

Per The Athletic's Jon Machota , Cowboys star quarterback Dak Prescott acknowledged his coach's change in demeanor, telling reporters that he's got a new chip on his shoulder after weeks of criticism.

"Definitely a hungry, pissed off version of Shotty," Prescott said after the game. "It's not like he's naive. It's not like he hadn't heard some noise about him, and whether it's calling the games or whatever doubt that's been out there. But we've got his back. He knows that. He's a guy that takes a lot of pride in his job, a lot of pride in his team."

Machota reported that Schottenheimer's time at the podium during his post-game press conference "lasted barely over four minutes. Something was off. His answers were much shorter than usual. Some were only a few words."

When Schottenheimer was asked about his curt responses, he said, "I'm great. Excited for our guys."

Schottenheimer came under fire after Dallas' slow start to the 2026 campaign. Still, at 3-4, the Cowboys are in second place in the NFC East, and they have a chance to climb the standings with matchups against the Arizona Cardinals (2-5) and Indianapolis Colts (2-5) up next.

Prescott added that he expects Schottenheimer to continue to bring some extra fire as he tries to silence his doubters.

"Everybody handles everything different, so I don't blame him to an extent. We've got his back," Prescott said. "More importantly, it's just about us going out there and executing on Sundays."

articles.body:
The fantasy football season nears the halfway point. And some players are still proving their worth . But looking ahead, here are the fantasy football defense and special teams rankings for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season.

It's another week where the byes come into play. The Texans, although they've been very disappointing, are off. Also taking a rest are the 49ers, Saints, and Giants. And that leaves some interesting teams at the top.

It's a good week to take a chance on the Bengals. They have a great matchup against the offensive emptiness of the Titans. In full fairness, the Titans showed a little bit of life against the Browns in a 27-24 loss in Week 7.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

But the Bengals really showed their teeth. They gave up 13 first-half points to the Ravens, but shut them down the rest of the way. Along the way, they had four sacks and an interception.

Edge rusher Boye Mafe has made a big difference for this Bengals defense, according to Pro Football Focus.

"Mafe starred against the Ravens, producing an initial 90.2 overall PFF grade — a mark that would set a new career high," Bradley Locker wrote. "His impact was most felt as a pass-rusher, generating five pressures and two sacks on a gaudy 23.1% pass-rush win rate over 27 pass-rushing snaps.

"Mafe's career-best outing in Week 7 punctuates what's been a revelatory season for the first-year Bengals. Through seven weeks, Mafe has produced an 88.9 overall PFF grade, the fourth-highest among edge rushers to play 200 or more snaps this season."

Another strong point for the Bengals has been their red zone work. They rank No. 3 in the NFL, allowing only 35% of opportunities to result in touchdowns, according to cleveland.com.

"I think they're playing with a lot of confidence," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said. "It's calls we review every week and do a really good job walking through, trying to practice them on Fridays, what we're gonna do."

And they succeeded against the Ravens despite being on the field a lot.

"Sometimes it's after long drives where you've been on the field yesterday for eight minutes," Taylor said. "And it's defeating because they've converted third downs and gotten big plays. And you got to overcome adversity, and then you got to just buckle up and hold them to a field goal. That's what we did twice yesterday. And that turned out to be really significant in the first half to hold them to those field goals and not touchdowns."

As for the Titans, Tony Pollard is coming off a big game with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns. Don't look for Pollard to be able to repeat that type of performance against the Bengals. That's true even though the Bengals have been below average against the run, ranking No. 18 with 116.3 yards allowed per game.

As high on the list are the Rams. They get a home game against the struggling Chargers. The Chargers rank No. 27 in the NFL with just 287.2 yards per game. They've struggled to get quarterback Justin Herbert rolling.

And the Rams seemed to find something on both sides of the ball last week against the Raiders.

Unfortunately, the Rams still don't know when Myles Garrett will be back on the field, according to a post on X by Nate Atkins.

"The Rams have not made a determination yet on whether or not to open the practice windows for Myles Garrett or Terrance Ferguson, per Sean McVay."

Even without Garrett, the Rams should have a shot at making some splash fantasy plays against the Chargers.

The Steelers' defense has been solid if nothing else. And they have a good matchup against the Browns this week. It should be a low-scoring game.

They are coming off a game where they held the Saints to 18 yards on 17 carries. Confidence is brimming , according to Post-Gazette.com.

"We have a lot of confidence in creating turnovers and creating those splash plays," said outside linebacker T.J. Watt. "We've done a really good job trying not to press too hard to make those plays happen, and they've been coming to us."

The Browns have been one of the most surprising teams in the NFL. But this could be the week the offense gets overwhelmed and can't keep up.

Another good fantasy pick this week is the Jaguars. They're coming off a bye week and have a matchup against the shaky Colts' offense. If they can keep Jonathan Taylor from cutting loose, they have a shot to make plays when the Colts pass the football.

Overall, the opportunity is there , according to rotoballer.com.

"The Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST has one of the best matchups of the week," Joey Pollizze wrote. "The Colts have had a hard time moving the ball this season. They rank 25th in EPA/play, 20th in points per game, and 24th in sacks allowed per game. Daniel Jones has also thrown an interception in six of seven contests, and Indianapolis has been held to under 24 points in four of the last five weeks."

Oh, you have to be brave to go here. But the Commanders have a nice matchup against an inept Eagles offense. With Saquon Barkley pulling up gimpy against the Cowboys on Monday, the Eagles can't exactly throw a scare into the Commanders.

What you're banking on is a good sack effort. The Commanders have been able to get better pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season. But they haven't finished a lot, with only 11 sacks on the season.

Another sleeper pick is the Browns. They get the Steelers this week. That's not a great matchup, but Aaron Rodgers is immobile. If the Browns can get pressure, they have a chance for a strong fantasy outing.

articles.title: Are the Minnesota Vikings really the NFL's best team? Brian Flores, Kyler Murray and question marks for the last unbeaten side
articles.summary: Defeats for the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers in Week 7 means the Minnesota Vikings are the NFL's final unbeaten team at 6-0; what has driven their perfect start to the 2026 season? And can Kevin O'Connell's side sustain their success to be genuine Super Bowl contenders?
articles.body:
Bill Belichick famously used to suggest that the season doesn't truly begin until Thanksgiving is out the way so, still a month shy of that mark, playoff forecasts feel a touch premature in what is shaping up as yet another wide-open campaign.

The Vikings are a perfect 6-0 at the top of a competitive NFC North division, though it ought to be remembered that the Indianapolis Colts flew out to an 8-2 mark last season only to lose seven straight and miss out on the postseason altogether. Momentum swings dangerously in the NFL; for now, Kevin O'Connell's side deserve their flowers.

They extended their winning start with a 16-10 victory over the Colts on Sunday, while the San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs were both dealt their first losses of the season by the Atlanta Falcons and Seattle Seahawks, respectively.

Minnesota's early success has featured wins over four teams with losing records in the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Miami Dolphins, New Orleans Saints and Colts, while they have taken down Championship-aspiring divisional rivals in both the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears - their victory over the latter serving up quintessential evidence as to their driving force.

That, of course, being Brian Flores' defense, the dominance of which is only further strengthening his case as the best assistant in football and surely nudging him closer to another head coaching job in the league, should he want one.

The Bears made a fierce statement in the opening week of the season when they dropped 59 points on the Carolina Panthers, before then running into Flores, against whom Ben Johnson's offense managed a solitary field goal in what had been billed as a clash of football masterminds.

Caleb Williams had been blitzed on 81.8 per cent of his dropbacks before exiting with an injury in the fourth quarter, the third-highest mark recorded in a game since at least 2018.

Flores would ramp up those numbers further this past weekend as the Vikings blitzed Daniel Jones on 85.2 per cent of dropbacks - the highest blitz rate by any defense in a game since the NextGen Stats era began in 2016. What's more, of that 85.2 per cent, they created pressure on 60.9 per cent of blitzes, which amounted to all four of their sacks in the game.

There is no defensive scheme in the league that comes close to being as aggressive as that of Flores', whose sending of the blitz serves as the nucleus to how he operates.

"I tell our guys all the time, 'If we're going to go down, we're going to go down a certain way. We're going to go down blitzing people,'" Flores said earlier this season.

Flores' defense ranks second only to the Seahawks in total yards allowed and passing yards allowed per game, while being 10th against the run and first in scoring, having surrendered just 12.3 points per game on average.

They are first in EPA/play (measuring down-to-down efficiency), second in dropback EPA and third in rush EPA, with a league-high success rate. In fact, the Vikings defense lead the NFL in EPA/play since Flores took over as defensive coordinator in 2023.

Their 74 points allowed this season is also the fewest of any team through six games since 2019, while their 21 sacks is tied for most in the league.

And as much as it is a reflection of Flores, it is also a credit to the depth and versatility he has when it comes to personnel on defense. Inside linebackers Blake Cashman and Eric Wilson have exemplified the strength of Flores' approach with the lateral speed, physicality downhill and play diagnosis in coverage to disguise their defense's intentions; their ability to rush the passer, to smother running backs and retreat off the line of scrimmage post-snap has become a nightmare for opposing offenses to ID them.

Cashman was unstoppable last time out with two sacks and five pressures on 12 rush attempts against the Colts, while Hall of Fame-bound veteran safety Harrison Smith became just the third player in history to record 40 interceptions and 20-plus sacks in his career behind Ronde Barber and Charles Woodson. He is a dream fit for Flores, who continues to squeeze every ounce of all-action football from the 37-year-old.

Dallas Turner, meanwhile, is stringing together a breakout year as the featured pass rusher on a unit designed for everybody to feast. He's assumed a heightened role this season after the departure of Jonathan Greenard.

Flores has become a master for controlled chaos, the unrivalled frequency of his blitzes tormenting teams when he decides to simulate rushers before dropping them into coverage. At times there could be eight or nine purple jerseys dotted across the line of scrimmage, only for two or three to drop in a game of guesswork.

According to ESPN Stats, the Vikings rank first in yards per attempt and yards per dropback when they rush just four men or fewer, evidencing their influence when not in blitzing scenarios.

"The problem for the offense is you don't have enough guys to block all those guys," said Sky Sports NFL 's Jeff Reinebold. "They're always plus one. But who that one is, you don't know!

"What they do a good job of is they'll step at the line of scrimmage and then get into their drop, so now as a quarterback or an offensive lineman or a running back, it's that he's up and then you've guessed wrong.

"It is a high risk defense because if you guess wrong on the other side you better have some guys who can cover. But what it does is it puts incredible mental pressure on the offense."

Is the Vikings' success sustainable? For as good as the defense has played, the answer to that questions likely rests on the shoulders of O'Connell's offense - which has so far failed to convince it can reward the efforts of Flores' unit with playoff-calibre performances. It is a reason to be cautious when it comes to Minnesota's perfect record.

The Vikings offense currently ranks third-worst in total yards, third-worst in passing, 12th in rushing yards, 23rd in points per game, 30th in EPA/play, last in success rate, 25th in dropback EPA, 27th in rush EPA, 30th in dropback success rate and 27th in rush success rate. It makes for ugly reading adjacent to Flores' attack dogs.

"I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," said O'Connell after the win over Indianapolis. "The 'far off' changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going."

Minnesota have jumped between quarterbacks in recent years, declining to follow up on Sam Darnold's career-resurrecting campaign in 2024, only to see him win a Super Bowl in Seattle last season.

They spent time with Carson Wentz under center and eventually decided 2024 first-round draft pick JJ McCarthy was not their future. Concidentally, for all O'Connell has come to be known as a quarterback whisperer, McCarthy just looked like a player reborn as the New York Giants beat the Houston Texans in the former No 10 picks' first start for Big Blue.

Kyler Murray arrived from the Cardinals this offseason tasked with proving himself as a legitimate answer at quarterback, having seen his career fizzle out in Arizona. So far he has underwhelmed, completing 83 of 125 passes for a 30th-ranked 812 yards and just three touchdowns to two interceptions.

It has amounted to 23 catches from just 31 targets for a 44th-ranked 302 yards through the air for Justin Jefferson. To put that into context, Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty has 34 catches from 45 targets for 312 yards.

Murray and O'Connell have a debilitating problem if they continue to fail in getting the ball to their best player, and perhaps the best receiver in the NFL.

Minnesota's 10 touchdowns are tied for the third-fewest in NFL history for a 6-0 team, per ESPN Stats; right now Brian Flores' defense is the Bugatti in the trailer park.

How long can the Vikings live by such glaring imbalance? Upcoming games against the 4-2 Lions, Josh Allen's 5-1 Buffalo Bills, the 4-3 Packers, Brock Purdy's 6-1 49ers and the rising Atlanta Falcons will deliver some better answers.

Are they the NFL's best team? No. But for now their blemish-free record suggests otherwise, spearheaded by their genius defensive architect.

articles.body:
Rapper Jay-Z will perform at halftime of Super Bowl LXI in February, the NFL announced on Monday.

Jay-Z is the head of Roc Nation, the music and entertainment company that, along with Apple Music, selects the Super Bowl halftime act each year. The 25-time Grammy-winning musician and media mogul is now set to perform at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on Sunday, Feb. 14, with the game airing on ESPN and ABC.

The first hip-hop artist to be inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, Jay-Z will perform a year after international pop icon Bad Bunny’s performance, which was widely panned by conservatives and President Trump.

Jay-Z is the second rapper in three years to serve as the Super Bowl halftime act, following Kendrick Lamar in 2025, whose performance dissing fellow rapper Drake went viral on social media for months after the show.

The Super Bowl halftime show also featured a hip-hop performance the last time it was in Los Angeles, as Snoop Dogg, Dr. Dre and Mary J. Blige combined their talents in an ode to West Coast rap and R&B.

“From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey,” Jay-Z said in a statement issued through the league. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.”

Bobby Belt of 105.3 The Fan in Dallas reported that Pickens played 12 fewer snaps than third-year wideout Ryan Flournoy, with most of his lost work coming in run situations after head coach Brian Schottenheimer called him out for his blocking last week.

Pickens was targeted just six times by Cowboys star quarterback Dak Prescott. Flournoy caught all four of his targets for 70 yards, while CeeDee Lamb led the way with five catches for 74 yards and two touchdowns on 12 targets. Dallas produced 204 yards on the ground, with starting running back Javonte Williams rushing for 155 yards and a touchdown.

Pickens now has 37 catches for 485 yards and two touchdowns this season, well behind last year's scorching pace. He's surpassed the 100-yard mark just once in seven games.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones downplayed the questions about Pickens' playing time, pointing out that all of the team's wide receivers were asked to do more in the run game.

"All of our receivers blocked well (Monday night). That's a credit to coaching. That's a point of emphasis," Jones said during his appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

Pickens is in a contract year, so he will try to get back to his usual production level when the Cowboys (3-4) fact the Arizona Cardinals (2-5) in Week 8.

articles.title: Return Of The 'X-Factor': Brian Branch Makes Lions A Legit Super Bowl Contender
articles.summary: The return of safety Brian Branch from last season's Achilles injury makes Detroit one of the NFL’s scariest teams — and a title contender.
articles.body: FORD FIELD (Detroit) — Sitting at his locker, Penei Sewell offered a simple response when asked about what Brian Branch’s return means for the Lions — not just to the defense, but to the team as a whole. The All-Pro offensive tackle pointed to early in the fourth quarter on Sunday, when the Packers faced a third-and-21 deep in their own territory. The Lions were up 17-14 and Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love fired a deep shot to his go-to target, Christian Watson. Branch, the 2024 Pro Bowl safety in his first game back from a torn Achilles last December, came flying across the middle of the field for a leaping interception. It was a massive play late in a tightly-contested affair, the Lions’ first division game of the season, and Detroit’s sideline erupted. The roar from the Ford Field crowd was deafening. "I mean, you guys heard that crowd," Sewell said of Branch. "You saw the team when he got that pick. I feel like that is self-explanatory." Let’s take Sewell’s words a big step further: The return of Brian Branch makes these Lions a legitimate Super Bowl contender. Let's also be clear: The Lions are still missing former All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph, who they expect to get back at some point this season from a knee injury. In the meantime, Branch can stabilize the secondary, which makes Detroit’s defense competent. And all these Lions need is competence on that side of the ball, given that they have arguably the NFL’s top offense. The interception by Branch, who spent the first six games of the season on the physically unable to perform list, highlighted the effort from a Lions defense that made timely stops against the Packers’ potent passing attack in Detroit's 20-17 win. "We all played a hell of a game, and I'm just proud to be a part of the secondary," Branch said. "We done been through a lot, and now it's time to hit the ground running." Detroit still has the NFL’s worst pass defense, and the Lions' inability to generate turnovers — they're tied for 26th with just six takeaways — has exacerbated their issues in the back end. But Branch’s presence immediately changes the calculus. He’s a big-time playmaker. In his first 44 NFL games, he has eight interceptions, 39 passes defensed, 20 tackles for loss and three forced fumbles. On a pitch count Sunday, Branch offered a glimpse of what he can give the Lions moving forward. In addition to the pick, he registered four tackles. "I thought he was running with a turbo. He was really running super fast into his gap, and it confused me, but that’s just who he is," Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes said. "Obviously, got to get used to knowing that B.B. is going to run to his gap. He’s a phenomenal person to have back for this team, this defense. "When the ball is in the air, going down deep, and I look up and I see No. 32, I’m almost 99.9 percent sure that it’s going to be his ball," Barnes continued. "I’ve witnessed it multiple times. … He’s a ball hawk." The 4-2 Lions, who host the undefeated Minnesota Vikings on Sunday (1 p.m. ET on FOX), have an enhanced confidence defensively with Branch on the field. "He just understands football so well," veteran cornerback D.J. Reed said. "He’s just overall a great player. I don’t think he has any weaknesses." Pro Bowl defensive end Aidan Hutchinson calls Branch the "tone-setter" of Detroit's defense. "That’s his X-factor right there," Hutchinson explained. "He can change a game by making a hit, forcing a fumble, doing a big splash play like [the interception]." And Branch’s return comes as Detroit is starting to figure it out as a collective defense. Sure, it wasn’t all pretty against the Packers on Sunday. The Lions allowed pass plays of 22, 27 and 28 yards on fourth-down attempts. They gave up a wide-open touchdown on a third-and-9. But Detroit forced a turnover on downs with Green Bay at the 7-yard line. Branch’s fourth-quarter interception bailed out the Lions’ offense, which had turned the ball over on downs inside the 10-yard line. The pick was preceded by an impressive pass breakup by backup cornerback Khalil Dorsey. Detroit also held Green Bay to a field goal on its penultimate possession, and defensive end DJ Wonnum got a hand on the 35-yard FG attempt on the Packers’ last drive. The Lions have now held opponents under 25 points in three of their past four games. And slowing down a dangerous Packers offense is a massive step in the right direction. "I thought our defense really, really stepped up, and they were the big story of this game," coach Dan Campbell said after Sunday's game. "I can see there is a confidence, there is a trust that's building with some of these guys. "The front's been doing a really good job. The backers have been playing pretty dang good, too, and the back end in spurts. But these last two games, we really stepped up. … We're challenging on some of these throws down the field. We're making it hard and there's nothing free, man. We're trying to defend every blade of grass, and that's what good defenses do." An improving defense that now has Branch back, one that's supported by an elite offense? Watch out, NFL. NFL Related StoriesNFL Best & Worst Week 72026 NFL Power RankingsNFL Week 7 All-Stars

articles.title: Jerry Jones says Cowboys would be interested in hiring Troy Aikman if 'Monday Night Football' contract stalls
articles.summary: It sounds like Jerry Jones would happily go after Troy Aikman if the former Cowboys quarterback is looking for a job.
articles.body:
If Troy Aikman finds himself out of a job after the 2026 NFL season, he won't stay unemployed for long. Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones spoke glowingly about Aikman during a radio appearance Tuesday, with the owner saying he would have interest in bringing Aikman back to the organization if he's looking for work.

Jones, 84, called Aikman "one of the hardest working, most focused people" he knows during an interview with 105.3 The Fan. While Jones said there were no immediate plans to bring Aikman in now, he added, " Don't rule it out. It's very possible ."

Jones' comments come amid reports of unrest between Aikman, his broadcast partner Joe Buck and ESPN. The reported feud stems from Aikman's contract situation. The former Cowboys quarterback is in his final year with ESPN and has yet to sign a long-term extension with the network to continue calling "Monday Night Football" games.

Things apparently came to a head in October, when Aikman and Buck got into a verbal altercation before a broadcast over Buck signing a massive, new extension with ESPN in September.

At the time, it was reported the network had yet to send a formal offer to Aikman.

When asked about the situation, Aikman declined to go into specifics, though did imply he was willing to court offers from other networks once his contract was up.

"I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens," Aikman said in October. "I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this year does hold with the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot might be."

Given Aikman's years of experience as a broadcaster, it's likely he would be a coveted free agent among other networks if he fails to come to a new deal with ESPN. That could complicate Jones' plans to try and bring Aikman back to the Cowboys. If the former quarterback still wants to broadcast games, he should have that opportunity.

But if Aikman decides he's ready for a change after almost three decades in the booth, the Cowboys make a lot of sense. Aikman starred with the franchise for his entire 12-year NFL career, leading the team to three Super Bowl titles and eventually making the Pro Football Hall of Fame. He's clearly still well-loved within the organization.

In order for Aikman to take a job with the Cowboys, he would almost certainly have to end his consulting gig with the Miami Dolphins. That probably shouldn't be viewed as a major barrier considering Aikman's previous relationship with the Cowboys.

It will likely be months before any significant progress is made on Aikman's next landing spot. Barring a surprising new deal, Aikman will have to wait for his ESPN contract to expire before multiple suitors come calling for his services. While many of those suitors will likely be other television networks, it certainly sounds like Jones will put in a call to his former quarterback.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes: 'Extra special' Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has proven he is one of the greatest athletes of his generation
articles.summary: Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds and Jeff Reinebold analyse the 'generational' mentality of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes on the latest episode of Inside the Huddle; watch Mahomes' Chiefs face the Denver Broncos live on Sky Sports NFL from 9.25pm this Sunday
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback endured a frustrating night on Sunday as his side saw their perfect start to the season come to an end in a 20-3 loss to the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Speaking on Inside the Huddle , Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds and Jeff Reinebold hailed further evidence of the 'generational' competitiveness and mentality that has amounted to three Super Bowl victories, five Super Bowl appearances and seven straight AFC Championship Game outings from 2018-2024.

Among the game's flashpoints was a third-quarter fumble by Mahomes himself, prompting a chaotic sequence in which he put his body on the line while chasing down the loose ball.

"I know he lost, but Patrick Mahomes is an incredible competitor," said Sky Sports NFL presenter Reynolds on Inside the Huddle . "I want to go back to Super Bowl 50, it was a fumble, Cam Newton stood there and didn't dive on the pile, watched the ball, just watched it, left it. It was a Super Bowl. We were very critical of him in that moment.

"There's a part in the game. It's 13-0 to Seattle. Mahomes gets absolutely slammed in the back by Derick Hall, fumbles the ball, ball's on the ground rolling towards the sideline. Mahomes chases it, gets tripped over by another defender, falls flat on his face, gets back up, dives, by which time, it's a melee then, there's offensive linemen, defensive linemen, he dives in there again, disappears under the bottom of the pile and comes out with the football.

"They kick a field goal, he gets the ball back, they're rolling a little bit, it gave them energy for a period. I just haven't seen that before, a quarterback so hungry, maybe at his own expense, to get after a football.

Mahomes and the Chiefs, thanks to a lot of help from marquee addition Kenneth Walker III, have rediscovered their spark on offense this year after Kansas City missed out on the playoffs for the first time since 2014 last season.

It had been something of a team reborn ahead of their defeat in Seattle, Mahomes teasing shades of his best once more after undergoing knee surgery last year.

"I've seen him practice as well at Chiefs training camp three, four times, and on a couple of those occasions there aren't even fans watching," Reynolds continued. "Bad weather forced the Chiefs inside, in their indoor facility. So it's just a handful of media there. He competes all the time. I mean, all the time. It's not like he's getting up for the fans when they're out on the practice field in training camp, indoor facility, no one watching.

"Ask him for a race or game of cards in the locker room, bet he's the same way. There's just some people that are just wired different. That's how they get to where they are."

Reinebold likened Mahomes' mindset to that of NBA icons Kobe Bryant and Michael Jordan, insisting his will to win and competitive drive have been just as important as his arm talent and intelligence in fuelling his rise to greatness.

"There are a lot of reasons why Pat Mahomes is one of the top quarterbacks that we've seen in our generation," said Reinebold. I think I can say that fairly. He's got all the physical tools, but it's the intangible things, right? His football intelligence, and his competitive heart. That was on display in that game. That's how you get your team to rally, when they see you as the quarterback putting yourself at risk for the team, that speaks volumes to that football team.

"How can you as an offensive lineman or a receiver or another position player not give it up when you see the best quarterback in our generation putting himself at risk for the football? I love the fact that he competes as hard as he does. He doesn't have to prove anything to anybody because we've watched him play hurt over his career."

Mahomes, whose Chiefs play the Denver Broncos live on Sky Sports this weekend, is one of just five quarterbacks in history to win three or more Super Bowls as a starter, is a two-time MVP, a three-time Super Bowl MVP and holds NFL records in total single-season yards by a quarterback (5,608) and career passing yards per game (285.2).

"The playoff game where he could barely walk and he went out and finished the game and won the game for his football team. This guy is an extra special talent," Reinebold continued.

"That's probably a common thread among all of the great athletes of of the day. You talk about Mamba Mentality with Kobe Bryant. He wrote books about how competitive he was and how intense his workouts were, I'm sure [Cristiano] Ronaldo and all the great ones have that same thread running through them that they're intensely competitive about everything.

"Michael Jordan was famous that he wanted to compete at everything, when they would go on on trips the luggage would come on the carousel, he'd bet his luggage came off first. That's how competitive those guys are."

articles.title: “Fix the Chargers”: Was it appropriate to ask Madison Beer, Justin Herbert’s fiancée, this on stage at Disneyland?
articles.summary: Madison Beer probably wasn't expecting football advice while standing on a stage at Disneyland. But one NFL fan had a very specific request for the singer.
articles.body: Madison Beer probably wasn't expecting football advice while standing on a stage at Disneyland. But one NFL fan had a very specific request for the singer. Beer, who is engaged to Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, found herself in an unexpected situation when the fan commented something about her fiance’s team during her Disneyland appearance. The singer responded with a smile and a two-handed shrug.Madison Beer gets asked to “fix the chargers” while on stage at Disneyland as Justin Herbert's team sits at 0-6The fan had a very specific request for the singer: “Fix the Chargers!” Funny? Could be. Uncalled? DefinitelyConsidering how the Chargers' season has gone so far, it's not hard to understand why a fan might be frustrated but passing a comment like that to the fiance might be a little too much, even as a joke.The Chargers are having a nightmare start to the 2026 NFL season. The team entered its Week 7 bye with a 0-6 record, leaving fans waiting for their first win. Their problems have been particularly noticeable on offense. Through six games, the Chargers averaged just 15 points per game and ranked 30th in that category. They also ranked last in the league in expected points added per play, according to the team's bye-week breakdown.Herbert has also been under pressure. The quarterback recorded 10 turnovers through the first six games, including eight interceptions, while injuries along the offensive line have made things even more difficult.The team's struggles have naturally put the spotlight on Herbert, head coach Jim Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. After the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, Harbaugh acknowledged that the offense needed serious improvement. But the Disneyland moment brought the frustration somewhere rather unexpected.Madison Beer gets pulled into the football conversationHer relationship with Herbert means that she can sometimes find herself connected to the Chargers' ups and downs. The couple announced their engagement on July 28, 2026, and their relationship has attracted attention from both music and football fans. That connection likely explains why the fan decided to direct the comment at Beer in the first place.The remark might have been made in a playful spirit, and the clip alone doesn't establish whether the fan was seriously criticizing her or simply trying to get a reaction. Still, there's a difference between joking about a quarterback's performance and asking his fiancée to take responsibility for it.Was the fan's comment fair?That's where the moment gets a little more interesting. NFL fans have every reason to be vocal about a team's performance, especially when a season begins with six straight losses. Supporting a struggling franchise can test anyone's patience.But Beer isn't responsible for the Chargers' record, and she shouldn't have to answer for Herbert's performances. Her shrug was perhaps the perfect response. She acknowledged the moment without pretending she had a solution.For Chargers fans, the real fix will have to come on the football field. articles.title: Jerry Jones 'Could and Would' Hire Troy Aikman to Work for Cowboys, 'It's That Simple'
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones confirmed that he'd be interested in hiring ESPN color commentator and former star quarterback Troy Aikman to a front office role.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones confirmed that he'd be interested in hiring ESPN color commentator and former star quarterback Troy Aikman to a front office role.

"Yeah," Jones said during a Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas (h/t Mark Maske of Front Office Sports). "Yes, I could and would. And so it's that simple because I do think that much of him, with his basic command and understanding and knowledge of NFL football. And so he certainly is qualified to do any of the things that have been mentioned. And I think he's outstanding at what he focuses on right now, and that's giving the story, the narration of the football games of all teams."

Aikman is currently under contract with ESPN, although he previously revealed that he'll be a "free agent" at the end of the 2026 NFL season.

He was spotted talking with Jones prior to the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.

Jones also praised Aikman when discussing the possibility of a shift from broadcasting to front office work on Wednesday.

"Troy is very capable and he's so, really relatively speaking, he's in his youth as careers go," Jones told reporters. "He's very capable of doing any one of a number of things, certainly anything to do with football. I don't know of any area, short of getting back out on the field, I don't know of any area that Troy Aikman wouldn't be qualified and competent to go into."

Aikman, who spent all 12 years of his Hall of Fame career in Dallas, later expressed his appreciation for Jones' praise.

"This week he said some really kind things, which meant a lot to me, quite honestly," Aikman told Mike Fisher of Cowboys Roundtable regarding Jones (h/t Maske ). "So, yeah, I would welcome any conversation with Jerry. And quite honestly I don't know if there would be or if there ever would be an opportunity. But if Jerry came to me and felt that, in his heart, I could lend some services that would help make them better, I would. I'd have a hard time not taking a good look at that."

While Aikman has primarily served as a color commentator since 2001, he also spent time as a consultant for the Miami Dolphins last offseason.

The 59-year-old assisted the Dolphins in their search for a new general manager and head coach before Jon-Eric Sullivan and Jeff Hafley were hired for each respective position.

As for the Cowboys, they currently sit at 3-4 as they attempt to avoid missing the playoffs for the third consecutive season.

articles.title: Grading the trade: Colts deal Quenton Nelson, who could be major upgrade for Seahawks
articles.summary: The Colts felt compelled to trade their long-time Pro Bowl guard, and the Seahawks were more than happy to add a tone-setting veteran.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline is still two weeks away, but the deals are starting to roll.

The Colts sent offensive guard Quenton Nelson, an eight-time Pro Bowler, to the Seattle Seahawks in exchange for a third-round draft pick in 2027 and a fifth-rounder in 2028.

The trade has major implications for both teams and could signal more future activity from each club. It also takes one of the best blocking pieces off the market for now.

Who got the better end of the trade? Let's dive in.

Colts made tough call on Nelson, putting emotion to the side

The firing of general manager Chris Ballard was the first indicator that the Colts' mentality had shifted this season. At 2-2, the team was still very much in the thick of things. After three straight losses, the Colts can't be viewed as contenders, especially as head coach Shane Steichen is having to answer questions about QB Daniel Jones' job security as the team's starter.

So trading away assets feels like a reasonable approach, especially for an expiring-contract player who's on the back half of his career such as Nelson. But on the other hand, Nelson was also a lifelong Colt who was a massive favorite of late team owner Jim Irsay and still one of the team's most dependable, rock-steady players and leaders.

Trading Nelson is an indication that no Colt should feel untouchable with Ed Dodds replacing Ballard (for now) and Carlie Irsay-Gordon taking over the team's operations from her father. Irsay-Gordon has routinely been on broadcasts doing an audit (or a triage?) of the team's game-day operations and clearly is taking her role seriously.

The Colts have other players who are far less tethered to the organization who also soon could be moved. Lacking a first-round draft pick next year from the Sauce Gardner trade, the Colts are trying to recoup as much draft-pick value as possible before the spring. With Jones' struggles, along with the Colts' apparent lack of trust in Anthony Richardson Sr., the team almost certainly will be going QB hunting in the offseason.

The return in value might feel low for a player of Nelson's talent and reputation. But given his age (turning 31 in March), contract status and positional value, the price feels adequate. For comparison, the Chiefs traded a 32-year-old Joe Thuney — in the final year of an expensive deal — to the Bears for a 2026 fourth-round pick in March 2025. Apples to apples, the Colts got plenty more in return.

The Colts were slated to have more than $60 million in salary cap space prior to the Nelson deal, so this opens them up to be even bigger players in free agency. Trading off more assets and dealing with Jones' contract in the offseason figures to open up even more space and flexibility.

It also indicates the depth of the rebuild facing Irsay-Gordon and whoever lands the full-time GM job. You could argue that after the Nelson trade, Jonathan Taylor is the only elite offensive player remaining — and Taylor's name has come up in trade rumors. ( Just ask Taylor's wife .) Indy's defense might also lose a few pieces in the coming weeks.

Dealing Nelson makes financial sense. It's probably the right thing to do, considering the circumstances. But it's also a painful loss that opens up old wounds from the team's recent missteps, and those don't always heal quickly.

In go-for-it mode again, Seahawks upgrade major offensive sore spot

The Seahawks' dominant victory over the Chiefs Sunday night was a good reminder of just how tough Seattle can still be. The Nelson trade figures to only improve their chances of winning a second straight Super Bowl.

That's, of course, far from a given. But with a dominant defense and an offense that has been incomplete to this point, adding known quantities at needed positions feels like a savvy stroke by GM John Schneider.

Nelson also embodies the toughness that head coach Mike Macdonald wants coursing through his roster's veins. There's also an argument to be made that Nelson joining an established contender could light a fire under him. The Colts have gone 31-43-1 over the past five seasons, including this one, and haven't made the postseason since the 2020 campaign.

Generally speaking, Nelson is probably a more efficient run blocker than pass protector, although it's hard to say that he's anything less than above average in the latter department. He hasn't been credited with allowing a sack since Week 14 of last season, per PFF, and has allowed a mere six pressures all season.

Nelson has also continued being the road grader in the run game he had been for years.

The Seahawks have trotted out multiple right guards this season, and it's been a clear sore spot on offense. Neither Christian Haynes nor Anthony Bradford claimed the job, necessitating the Nelson trade.

Nelson has played every snap of his NFL career at left guard. An easy fix would be to move Grey Zabel to the right side, which is where he played in college. That maneuver could actually upgrade both guard spots and have a cumulative effect for what's been an inconsistent run game to date this season.

The Seahawks have now traded away their original third-, fourth-, sixth- and seventh-round picks in 2027, as well as their fifth- and seventh-rounders in 2028. On the surface, that might look sparse. But the Seahawks are slated to receive four mid-round compensatory picks next spring, and they'll receive a third-round pick for executive Nolan Teasley being named Vikings general manager.

That makes the cost of the Nelson trade more palatable. Plus, when you consider that there reportedly were multiple suitors for Nelson, chalk it up as a win the Colts didn't hold out for a second-round pick in return.

Given the stage of his career and his contract status, this could end up being a fairly pricy rental — and that potential cost must be baked into the team's grade. But if Nelson plays to his expected level, or even above the level he's played at this season, and the Seahawks remain a title contender, it would be hard to label this as anything but a win.

It's hard to knock a team for a go-for-it move that appears to be a great fit, both on a football and a cultural level.
