articles.title: Giants' J.J. McCarthy Explains 'Corny' Reason for Not Wearing Eye Black vs. C.J. Stroud, Texans
articles.summary: Keen observers may have noticed New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy wasn't wearing his trademark eye black when making his first start for the team. The explanation goes back to his college rivalry with Ohio State.
articles.body:
Keen observers may have noticed New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy wasn't wearing his trademark eye black when making his first start for the team. The explanation goes back to his college rivalry with Ohio State.

McCarthy made a point to not put on eye black when playing against the Buckeyes as part of a wider grudge . He took the same approach against the Houston Texans in Week 7 since former Buckeyes star C.J. Stroud is their starting quarterback.

"Yeah, it is a little corny," he said, per The Athletic's Charlotte Carroll . "Don't get me wrong, but … you know, I guess I'm a corny guy. I took it personal in high school, growing up an Ohio State fan, like a die-hard Ohio State fan. I had the comforter, had the Fatheads, everything. And (it was) just a little disappointing situation. (So) at the end of the day, that's just something that I'll continue against all Buckeyes."

Beyond just the longstanding bad blood between OSU and Michigan, McCarthy took exception to Buckeyes coach Ryan Day getting a commitment from fellow 2021 recruit Kyle McCord. Day had purportedly pledged to wait much longer before he settled on a QB during that cycle.

McCathy still hasn't forgotten the perceived slight.

Maybe the extra edge helped the third-year signal-caller against the Texans. He went 20-of-28 for 252 yards in a 27-21 overtime victory. It was one of his best performances in the NFL.

McCarthy signaled the eye black will return, though, with the Philadelphia Eagles next up for the Giants. He'll likely leave the eye black in the locker only when he's facing off with Stroud or "unless Ryan Day comes up to the NFL."

articles.title: Caleb Williams vs. Drake Maye Voted on by NFL Personnel, Results Revealed After Bears Beat Patriots
articles.summary: Before the Chicago Bears defeated the New England Patriots last Thursday, 30-24, Albert Breer of SI.com polled 17 coaches and executives from around the NFL about whether they'd prefer to build their franchise around Caleb Williams or Drake Maye.
articles.body:
Before the Chicago Bears defeated the New England Patriots last Thursday, 30-24, Albert Breer of SI.com polled 17 coaches and executives from around the NFL about whether they'd prefer to build their franchise around Caleb Williams or Drake Maye.

Williams won out by a 12-5 margin, with Breer noting that his "ceiling, creativity and early record of clutch play" were the traits most cited in that decision.

"You call a perfect D, and still get beat, just like Josh [Allen] and [Patrick] Mahomes," an assistant general manager told him.

Maye, meanwhile, was preferred by some for his "personality and sustainability."

"Drake, but it's close," an offensive coordinator noted. "Drake appears to me to be a little ahead of Caleb operating in the pocket and getting through progressions in the passing game, and still has athleticism to create. Caleb has great athleticism/speed and arm strength but is maybe a little less consistent. ... Both are going to end up being really good."

Both players already led their respective franchises to a playoff berth last season, and both were fantastic on Thursday night, with Williams (308 passing yards, two touchdowns, no turnovers, 18 rushing yards) slightly getting the better of Maye (321 passing yards, two touchdowns, on interception, 26 yards and a score on the ground). The Bears and Pats are in good hands.

articles.title: What on earth happened to this Eagles defense?
articles.summary: The Eagles defense was supposed to be loaded with stars. They’ve been duds thus far.
articles.body:
We all knew the offense was going to be problematic.

Sean Mannion's new scheme would take time to get on its feet. Jalen Hurts would need to acclimate himself to it, the offensive line's health was a question mark, and there didn't appear to be many great answers at wide receiver. The prevailing wisdom was, if the Eagles were going to survive some early season growing pains from the offense, the defense would have to do a little more.

But after so much offensive futility over the first six weeks, Hurts' season ending blood clots, being forced to spend more time on the field than almost any other defense in the NFL and lugging around a 2-4 record, it appeared as if the effort dam broke for Vic Fangio's unit in the Eagles' embarrassing 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday Night Football.

Ironically, the offense actually showed a pulse for the first time all season. Tanner McKee is a backup quarterback for a reason, but he played pretty well through three quarters. After a really nice touchdown drive coming out of halftime gave the Eagles a 21-20 lead, the defense offered about as much resistance as single-ply Dollar Store toilet paper.

It's fair to say the defense has been far more disappointing than the offense through seven ugly weeks of football. Worse yet, it sure looked like they gave up on Monday night. Former Cowboys coach Wade Phillips summed it up best on ESPN's Manning Cast.

The numbers are disgusting, especially for a unit with this much high-priced, and soon-to-be high priced, talent on it.

They have given up the 6th-most yards per game (371.3), 7th-most passing yards per game (239.9), and 6th-most rushing yards per game (131.4). That they are only 12th-worst in points per game allowed (25.0) is a bit of a miracle, thanks to a couple key goal line stands against Jacksonville and the Rams. They have a mere three interceptions and are the only team in the league without a fumble recovery. Those three total takeaways are tied with the Colts for fewest in the league.

The Eagles' 28.1% pressure rate is 10th-worst, they have the 9th-fewest total pressures, and are 2nd-worst in sacks per game (1.1).

What's worse, there are no injury excuses on the defensive side of the ball, certainly not against Dallas. While they missed Nolan Smith (concussion) on the edge rushing the passer, there was more than enough there to hold down the fort. Jalyx Hunt and Jonathan Greenard returned to the lineup, joining a group of tackles thought to be the best trio in the NFL.

Instead, a Dallas running game that ranked 30th in the league coming into the Linc, ran for 204 yards on 38 carries, a 5.37 yard per carry average. Dak Prescott not only wasn't sacked, he wasn't even threatened.

Bear in mind, this is a defensive line with Greenard ($25.2), Jalen Carter ($24.4) and Jordan Davis ($20.5) making a combined $70.1 million this season. Carter has 3 sacks and 18 tackles in seven games. Greenard has one tackle and one QB hit in four games. Davis has 27 tackles and 0.5 sacks.

Remember Jalyx Hunt, the guy everyone swore up and down was due for a monster season and huge contract based off his summer reps? He remains without a sack and has 4 QB hits and 17 tackles. The other up-and-comer, Moro Ojomo, has no sacks, 3 QB hits and 18 tackles. They're not exactly playing themselves into big money deals. Only Smith has shown up this, leading all team edge rushers with 3 sacks, 3 QB hits and 4 tackles for loss.

Zack Baun and Quinyon Mitchell continue to play well, but the middle of the defense is missing safety Reed Blankenship's steady play and Nakobe Dean's athleticism and team leadership. Jeremiah Trotter, Jr. is now splitting time with last year's first round pick, Jihaad Campbell, who has disappointed in a larger role this season. The safeties have been a disaster, and Riq Woolen has been extremely uneven.

The decline in play from slot corner Cooper DeJean is particularly startling. He's likely to get a big money extension at some point, but he's putting it in jeopardy as he has suddenly begun missing a ton of tackles and finding himself at the center of defensive miscommunications that have led to big plays over the last few weeks.

Part of the problem is how much Fangio's unit has been on the field. Through their first seven games, the Eagles' defense has been on the field for 67.3 plays per game, 4th-most in the NFL. That's due to the offense leading the league in 3-and-outs. The defense has been on the field an average time of possession of 32:19. Only the Titans' defense has been out on the field longer.

However, on Monday night, the offense was holding its own. They gave the defense a shot to keep them in the game, but they couldn't keep up with Prescott and the Dallas offense. It was too much to ask.

It shouldn't have been. The defensive side of the ball is where all the money is.

So now, at 2-5, the Eagles' season is likely over. Even in a weak NFC East, it's clear they don't have the horses on offense, and it's clear something is amiss defensively. Howie Roseman should be a seller at the trade deadline in two weeks. At that time, it's possible some of these contributors on defense will be playing somewhere else.

For now, it's one of the most disappointing performances by any Eagles unit in recent memory.

articles.title: Texans GM Nick Caserio has had 'conversations' with ahead of trade deadline
articles.summary: Houston Texans general manager Nick Caserio has had "conversations" with other teams ahead of the NFL's trade deadline.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans have been active in the trade market, trading for wide receiver Kayshon Boutte before the start of the season and trading for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. ahead of the mid-season deadline.

There is still time before the trade deadline and Texans general manager Nick Caserio said he has had "conversations" about more trades, both internally grabbing someone or potentially shopping someone out.

"Every opportunity we'll look at it. If it makes sense, great. If not, so...we've had conversations. We've talked to most of the league here," Caserio said. "Teams have started to reach out here a little bit trying to figure out, like, 'What are you looking for? Where is the surplus? Where do you potentially have a need?' We'll always be open-minded. We're not going to eliminate anything. We'll listen, do what we feel makes the most sense. As it pertains to the offensive line, probably been a little bit up and down. At times it has been okay. At times it can be better. I think we have talked about this internally at different points."

There are numerous players across the NFL who could be available before the deadline. While intra-division trades are rare, Houston's AFC South rival, the Indianapolis Colts , appear to be sellers given their season and could be willing to trade running back Jonathan Taylor. If the Texans could acquire a running back like Taylor with their current offense, they could be a real contender.

Multiple players on defense are also expected to be available for trades, although the Texans do not lack defensive talent. Their problem so far this season has been execution. The defense this year is made up of most of the same players as last year; Houston's defense was one of the best in the NFL in 2025.

"We just got to do a better job of staying at task, staying finished. Again, we have a number of players at that position. Eleven offensive linemen on the roster. Probably as much as any. Some guys that have been injured, some guys that are coming back. We'll look at it and try to figure out and figure out if it's the best five. If not, let's try to do something else."

articles.title: New NFL Draft Rumors Update Buzz on C.J. Carr, Mensah, Mestemaker Amid Sayin, Dante Moore Injuries
articles.summary: Notre Dame quarterback C.J. Carr and Oklahoma State passer Drew Mestemaker have reportedly seen their stock rise for the 2027 NFL draft.
articles.body:
Notre Dame quarterback C.J. Carr and Oklahoma State passer Drew Mestemaker have reportedly seen their stock rise for the 2027 NFL draft.

According to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer , Carr and Mestemaker are "hitting November as the college quarterbacks with the most momentum within the NFL scouting community."

Breer also reported that Miami signal-caller Darian Mensah has "a chance" to be one of the top passers selected in next year's draft, but "questions remain on the ceiling."

Ohio State's Julian Sayin and Oregon's Dante Moore were expected to be among the top quarterbacks in the 2027 draft class, but they've both dealt with health issues during their respective 2026 campaigns.

Sayin suffered an injury to his throwing arm that could sideline him for the rest of the season, while Moore has been ruled out for the remainder of the year due to a concussion .

As for Carr, he's thrived through his first seven starts of the season. He's completed 66.8 percent of his throws for 1,639 yards and 16 touchdowns compared to just one interception.

Mestemaker has spearheaded a high-powered Oklahoma State offense, completing 65.7 percent of his passes for 2,326 yards and 20 touchdowns while getting picked off six times in seven games.

Meanwhile, Mensah has been a key piece of a Miami squad that sat at No. 1 in the latest AP Top 25 poll with a perfect 7-0 record.

He's thrown for 2,151 yards and 22 touchdowns to go along with one interception across seven appearances. Mensah's 81.4 completion percentage is also the highest mark in the country.

In the latest mock draft from Bleacher Report's NFL Scouting Department, Mestemaker was the first quarterback projected to be picked after he was taken off the board with the No. 3 overall choice.

articles.title: Dante Moore Compared to Packers' Jordan Love, Deemed '1st-Round Talent' by NFL Insider Amid Injury
articles.summary: Despite Oregon quarterback Dante Moore having his 2026 season cut short by a concussion, he's still viewed by some as one of the top signal-callers in the 2027 NFL draft.
articles.body:
Despite Oregon quarterback Dante Moore having his 2026 season cut short by a concussion, he's still viewed by some as one of the top signal-callers in the 2027 NFL draft.

Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer spoke to two college scouting directors and a director of player personnel who've evaluated Moore. Despite being left wanting more, they agreed that he has enough skills to impress NFL scouts.

"He's got a lot of arm talent," the director of player personnel, who compared him to Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love, told Breer. "First-round arm talent. He's accurate. Not a super impressive athlete, not very fast, but I really like the way he throws from the pocket."

Oregon head coach Dan Lanning announced on Monday that Moore is not expected to return this season as he continues his recovery from a concussion suffered in Week 4 against USC. Moore likely would've been considered a top-two quarterback in the 2026 NFL draft, but his stock hasn't taken too much of a hit to knock him out of the first round in 2027.

"He's a really talented passer—smooth, fluid, accurate," one of the college directors said. "He's just above the line athletically. He's not great, but it's not a hindrance. [C.J.] Carr and [Drew] Mestemaker are better athletes, [Fernando] Mendoza, [Ty] Simpson are better athletes. But it's not a major concern. He can process; he's smart. I think he's tough, a good player, a starting quarterback. He'll go in the first round, maybe not top 10. … Good, not great strength, that's just above the line, too. His superpower is his accuracy."

"He's a talented passer, good arm, smooth mechanics," the other college director said. "He's not dynamic, but a good athlete who can throw to all three levels, can throw on the move. I would've liked to see more, answering the bell and playing well in big games. He didn't get those opportunities. … He had a new coordinator, a new system, and never really got into the year with it. There are certainly a lot of questions, a lot to be figured out."

The director of player personnel added that he'd "want to sit down with the kid to dig further into" his character.

"Moore has a great reputation as a teammate and is considered to have a high football IQ," Breer stated. "But team leadership will certainly look further into the decision now to walk away from college football, which Lanning implied was out of Moore's control after Moore had returned to practice."

Still, Moore will have the chance to impress during the pre-draft process.

"He's gonna have to ace the spring process, which I think he will," the first college director said. "He's a really talented thrower, and routes on air, in shorts, he'll look good."
